   `solvent_ratios`、`additives` 等）是否显式填写，绝不用于表达“某项性能必须被报告”。
   禁止把“capacity retention … must be reported”写成
   `"kind": "field_presence", "field": "additives"` 这类把性能指标错配到配方字段的约束。
   ```json
   {
     "request": {
       "candidates": candidates,
       "constraint_records": [
         {
           "constraint_id": "temp-low",
           "description": "operating temperature ≤ -20°C",
           "kind": "temperature",
           "operator": "<=",
           "value": -20,
           "unit": "°C",
           "required_evidence_scope": "candidate_same_paper",
           "can_replan": true,
           "search_hint": "find low-temperature cycling evidence"
         },
         {
           "constraint_id": "electrode-hard-carbon",
           "description": "hard carbon anode",
           "kind": "electrode_material",
           "evidence_terms": ["hard carbon", "hard-carbon"],
           "required_evidence_scope": "candidate_same_paper",
           "can_replan": true,
           "search_hint": "find hard carbon anode evidence"
         },
         {
           "constraint_id": "cell-half",
           "description": "sodium half-cell configuration",
           "kind": "cell_configuration",
           "evidence_terms": ["half-cell", "half cell", "Na||HC", "HC||Na", "pure Na"],
           "required_evidence_scope": "candidate_same_paper",
           "can_replan": true,
           "search_hint": "find half-cell configuration evidence"
         },
         {
           "constraint_id": "field-concentration",
           "description": "explicit salt concentration must be present",
           "kind": "field_presence",
           "field": "concentration_mol_l",
           "required_evidence_scope": "candidate_same_paper",
           "can_replan": false
         },
         {
           "constraint_id": "salt-napf6",
           "description": "NaPF6 as salt",
           "kind": "required_component",
           "value": "NaPF6",
           "required_evidence_scope": "candidate_same_paper",
           "can_replan": true,
           "search_hint": "find NaPF6 electrolyte evidence"
         },
         {
           "constraint_id": "solvent-thf",
           "description": "THF as solvent",
           "kind": "required_component",
           "value": "THF",
           "required_evidence_scope": "candidate_same_paper",
           "can_replan": true,
           "search_hint": "find THF solvent evidence"
         }
       ]
     }
   }
   ```
   定性或断言型要求（如“无集流体/壳体腐蚀被观测到”“无析钠/无枝晶”“提高首圈库仑效率”
   “该添加剂抑制产气”）不得写成 `mechanism_keyword` 关键词表——关键词命中分不清
   “发生腐蚀”与“未发生腐蚀”。改用 `kind: "evidence_claim"`：在 `claim` 里用一句
   用户原话写出对单个候选须成立的断言，在 `claim_verdicts` 里**逐候选**给出判定。
   语义判断（这段原文是否为该候选建立或推翻该断言）由你负责；程序只做两件可机械
   核验的事：判定须指向本次请求的候选，`quote` 须在该候选证据正文中逐字存在。
   因此措辞、否定、同义称呼的变化都不影响判定，你只需如实读原文：
   - `supported`：有原文明确为该候选建立断言，附 `chunk_id` 与逐字 `quote`；
   - `refuted`：有原文明确反驳（如原文说“会持续腐蚀铝箔”），附 `chunk_id` 与逐字 `quote`；
   - `not_found`：检索到的证据未直接提及，如实填写，由补证机制驱动下一轮检索。
   背景介绍、他人体系的结果、无实验支撑的预测都不算 `supported`。例如：
   ```json
   {
     "constraint_id": "no-corrosion",
     "description": "no current-collector or case corrosion observed",
     "kind": "evidence_claim",
     "claim": "该候选电解液不腐蚀铝箔或钢壳",
     "claim_verdicts": [
       {
         "candidate_id": "candidate-1",
         "verdict": "refuted",
         "chunk_id": "fan2024::sec3",
         "quote": "the single NaFSI system can continuously corrode aluminum foil and stainless steel sheets",
         "basis": "原文明确说明单盐 NaFSI 会持续腐蚀铝箔与不锈钢，与该断言相反。"
       }
     ],
     "can_replan": true,
     "search_hint": "find corrosion test evidence for the candidate electrolyte"
   }
   ```
   `evidence_claim` 不得把 `required_evidence_scope` 设为 `component` 或 `background`：
   断言必须由候选自身绑定的证据支持，不能借用别篇论文或背景段落的措辞。
   给出 `supported` 前，逐句核对引文是否真正支持所写断言。引文必须从指定
   `chunk_id` 返回的原文复制，不能把题名、摘要或另一块文字放在该块的标识下。
   配方、测试条件和性能必须对应同一候选；一种优点不能替代另一项目标的证据。
   成本动机与价格比较分别表述，安全性或无氟组成不能自行推导出成本优势。
   `basis` 说明原句与断言的推理关系，不得以重复断言代替理由。程序核验引文
   存在及归属，不代替科学含义判断；证据未支持完整断言时应补证或保留 `not_found`。
   `criteria`/`target_conditions` 仅用于兼容旧调用方；新设计任务必须优先使用
   `constraint_records`，避免 evaluator 再从自由文本猜测硬约束。

   `required_evidence_kinds` 描述的是**支持记录本身的语义角色**，不是实验条件元数据。
   数值性能约束通常只要求 `property`；温度、电极、循环数等共同实例化条件应由该
   observation 的 `condition_scope` 和 `joint_context_requirements` 表达。除非硬约束本身
   确实要求一条独立的 condition 记录，否则不要把同一数值约束写成
   `required_evidence_kinds=["property", "condition"]`，否则会把“带条件上下文的性能观测”
   错当成缺少第二种证据角色。

   当两个及以上硬约束必须在**同一个目标实验上下文**中同时成立时，还必须显式写
   `joint_context_requirements`。分别在多个倍率测试的要求，按倍率分别建立条件组，
   每组的 `target_context.rate` 只填一个倍率。不能把 `0.5 C and 1 C` 当成一次测试的倍率。
   同一论文的不同盐浓度或溶剂比例必须分别对应其性能段，不能因来自同篇论文就互换结果。
   `target_context.cell_configuration` 使用条件检查器的外形名称 `pouch` 或 `coin`，
   不拼成 `pouch full cell` 这样的新标签。全电池要求另用 cell_configuration 检查条件
   和明确的正负极对验证；外形名称不能代替电极与全电池要求。
   它描述的是 evidence composition obligation，不要求所有
   支持证据拥有相同 `experiment_id`。`constraint_ids` 只能引用本次 `constraint_records`；
   `context_fields` 只列对联合决策真正相关的字段；`target_context` 只填写用户明确给出的
   目标条件，未知字段保持未知，禁止为了让 join 成立而补默认值。例如：
   ```json
   {
     "joint_context_requirements": [
       {
         "group_id": "low-temp-high-voltage",
         "constraint_ids": ["retention", "voltage"],
         "context_fields": ["temperature_c", "electrode"],
         "target_context": {"temperature_c": -20.0, "electrode": "hard carbon"},
         "can_replan": true,
         "search_hint": "find evidence satisfying both hard constraints at the target operating context"
       }
     ]
   }
   ```
   只有约束确实需要共同实例化时才声明 joint group；互不相关的硬约束不要强行合组。
   原文条件检查器分别识别 `electrode` 与 `cell_configuration`。涉及电池形式的用户要求
   使用独立的 cell_configuration 条件；只有相关观测明确提供该字段时，才作联合检查。
2. 检查用户输入与已有 ledger；存在组分、机理或替代体系缺口时，选择相应检索能力；
3. 如证据不足，再做有界补充检索：
   - 区分“已有候选缺少一段证据”和“已有候选并不适合目标”。先检查最相关论文；
     若当前候选仍不能满足目标，按缺口与完整目标检索其他候选，不反复只查原来的
     盐、溶剂或论文。新证据支持新的组成时重新组装候选，再用原任务的全部条件
     筛选。不能把不同候选的成本、工况或性能拼成一个通过的候选。
   - 尚未定位候选论文时，用 `search_literature_chunks` 做 1–2 次聚焦补充（`top_k=10`）；
   - 若返回结果已经给出明确 `paper_id`，且该论文与目标组分/机理直接相关但缺少显式配方或目标工况证据，必须对最相关的 1 篇论文调用一次 `search_paper_chunks(paper_id=..., query=..., top_k=8)`；`query` 用 4–8 个英文技术词描述缺失事实，不含作者名。将结果追加到 `evidence_chunks`，不得跨论文拼接配方与性能。
   - 对 **named-study / named-candidate** 设计任务，在进入 `query_formulation_space` 或
     `screen_formulations` 前，必须先取得同一论文中可追溯的配方/组成证据：至少有一条
     `evidence_kind="formulation"` 的记录能支持候选的盐、溶剂或添加剂组成。只有性能、温度、
     机理 chunk 不能建立候选配方归属；若当前只找到性能证据，应继续检索 formulation /
     composition 段落，而不是手工构造一个 `formulation_evidence_ids=[]` 的候选进入筛选。
4. 用户没有提供可评估候选时，调用 `query_formulation_space`，把目标转成：
   `{"request":{"task_type":"design","target_conditions":[...],"preferred_salts":[...],"preferred_solvents":[...],"preferred_additives":[...],"excluded_components":[...],"evidence_chunks": evidence_chunks,"max_candidates":3}}`；其中 `evidence_chunks` 必须传入前面检索实际返回、与目标最相关的最多 12 个 chunk，不得只传组分偏好而丢失文献上下文。工具会优先从这些同论文原文块组装候选，再使用 KG fallback；保留工具原样返回的 `candidates`。
   如果候选 evidence 只有 `chunk_id` 而 `text/excerpt` 为空，先调用
   `enrich_formulation_evidence({"request":{"candidates": candidates}})`，并用返回候选
   替换原列表；证据已有原文时不得为形式完整重复调用。enrichment 只补齐原文和元数据，
   必须保留原 evidence 的 `paper_id`、`evidence_kind` 和 `chunk_id`。
5. 若任务涉及离子电导率、温度下的传输性质或需要在多个 NaPF6–EC/EMC/PC 候选之间增加一个轻量定量参考，可在筛选前调用 `predict_formulation_conductivity`。只有以下两种情况允许数值预测：候选已有明确的 NaPF6/EC/EMC/PC 摩尔组成，或调用参数中的 `composition_inputs[candidate_id]` 显式给出 `component_mmol`、`molar_ratios` 或 `x_NaSalt/x_EC/x_PC`。现有 `solvent_ratios` 没有保存 v/v、w/w 或 molar 基准，因此**不得**仅凭“1 M + 1:1”之类字段推导模型输入。含其他盐、其他溶剂或添加剂的候选按域外处理；组成不足时保留 `insufficient_composition`，继续依赖文献/KG 证据。`model_predictions` 与 literature evidence 必须分开：模型预测可以辅助候选比较和后续实验优先级，但不能单独把实验事实型硬约束判为满足。
6. 只有需要形成配方推荐或明确 hold 时才调用 `screen_formulations`：
   传入当前候选和完整的结构化 `constraint_records`。旧文本字段用于兼容历史输入，
   新设计任务不能用它们替代结构化条件。
   每项 `claim_verdicts` 只判定本次 `candidates` 中实际提交的候选。候选集合变更时，
   同步更新各断言的候选判定，保持原任务的全部条件。工具返回参数错误后，修复
   指出的字段并重新提交完整请求，不得删去 `constraint_records` 或联合条件来消除报错。
    倍率与循环次数是两种不同测试，分别建立约束：指定 1 C 测试使用
    `{"kind":"c_rate","operator":"==","value":1,"unit":"C"}`；
    100 次循环使用 `{"kind":"minimum_cycles","value":100,"unit":"cycles"}`。
    指定 2.0–4.0 V 测试使用
    `{"kind":"voltage_window","operator":"==","value":[2.0,4.0],"unit":"V"}`。
    若任务要求 0.5 C 和 1 C，各自建立条件。
    双盐配方同时保存 `salts` 与 `salt_concentrations_mol_l`，分别记录各盐浓度；
    `concentration_mol_l` 表示总盐浓度，不得将它归给某一个盐。
    `solvent_ratio_basis` 按原文填写 `mass`、`volume` 或 `molar`；原文未说明时填
    `unknown`。不得把质量比例当成体积比例，或把溶剂比例直接当成包括盐的摩尔组成。
   若本任务已声明 `joint_context_requirements`，每次首次筛选和补证后的重新筛选都必须携带
   同一份 joint-context 合同；除非用户明确修改任务目标，否则不得在 re-screen 时删除、
   放宽 `context_fields` 或改写 `target_context`。runtime 会在字段被意外省略时保留上一版
   显式合同，但 Agent 仍应主动原样传递。
   保留工具原样返回的 `screening_results`、其中的 `criteria_evaluations` 与 `gaps`，
   不得手写分数、validations 或 scores。任何 `failed`、`insufficient_evidence` 或
   `unsupported` 判定都不得在报告中表述为性能已验证。
7. 旧调用方需要动作列表时，可调用 `optimize_formulations`：
   `{"candidates": candidates,"screening_results": screening_results,"request":{"task_type":"design","objectives":[目标性能...],"constraints":[用户硬约束...]}}`。
   不得同时传入 `validations` 或 `scores`。该兼容工具只翻译筛选后已经产生的
   `DecisionState`，不会再按 score 独立裁决；若 proposal 为
   `retrieve_more_evidence`，先执行对应的补充检索和重新筛选，再进入报告。
8. `DecisionState` 已达到 `recommend` 或 `hold` 后，必须**立即**调用 `synthesize_design_report`
   生成完整报告，并传入同一份原始 `screening_results`：
   `{"request":{"task_type":"design","question":用户问题,"evidence_chunks": evidence_chunks,"candidates": candidates,"screening_results": screening_results}}`。
   为提升 `claim_supported_ratio`，请在 `request.claims` 中提交**所有**被 `evidence_chunks` 直接支持的事实声明（`claim_type="fact"`），每条包含 `text`、对应 `chunk_id` 和唯一逐字原文引文 `evidence_quote`（必须从该 chunk 的 `content` 中逐字截取，且只出现一次）。**禁止为凑数量编造 claim**；若当前证据能直接支持的 claim 不足 2 条，应优先通过 `search_literature_chunks` 或 `search_paper_chunks` 补充检索，最多尝试 2 轮；若仍无法找到更多直接支持，则在报告中明确标注“证据不足”，并只提交已被验证的 claim。报告将渲染“已校验事实”小节，避免裁判从自由文本中抽取不被检索上下文支持的论断。
   报告要让使用者能安排下一步工作。用简明中文分别提交配方组成、文献的测试条件与数值、同条件基准配方的结果，并保留逐字引文。比例需说明质量比或体积比；浓度、添加剂用量不得省略或猜测。文献筛选不能写成新配方已由本智能体实验验证。
   当目标是某项性能时，报告必须包含已检索到的该项性能结果，不能只列出温度、
   电极和电压范围等测试设置。不同盐浓度、溶剂比例和添加剂分支的结果分别绑定到
   其配方。不得借用另一分支较好的结果；保留同一分支完整组成与性能已明确的候选，
   不必强求选取数值最高但组成仍缺失的分支。
   `next_steps` 按本次缺口列出具体核查或实验，包括要比较的配方、温度、倍率、电池类型和测量项目；这些是验证计划，不是已取得的结果。即使为 `hold`，也要展示已取得的候选资料、文献结果和暂缓原因，不得只写状态或检索流程。
   对没有数值判据的选材目标，`next_steps` 也要交代其验证状态。例如成本目标
   需要区分文献的成本动机与实际价格比较，不能因筛选通过就宣称全部目标已验证。
   性能类 `claims` 应优先包含与当前候选直接相连的实验结果，少选一般背景介绍。
   **关键纪律**：一旦 `screen_formulations` 返回 `hold` 或 `recommend`，**不得**再尝试重新构建候选、重新检索或输出自由文本；下一动作必须是 `synthesize_design_report`。若状态为 `search`，最多只做一轮补充检索 + 重新筛选，然后必须进入报告。
9. 直接输出报告全文，不得改写或截断。

## 退出纪律

- 不要求无条件调用所有工具；根据用户已有候选和结构化 evidence gaps 选择能力。
- `synthesize_design_report` 是终端编译能力。调用前必须已有终态 `DecisionState`；
  `search` 状态必须先按缺口补证或换候选，不能用固定工具次数代替状态判断。
- `recommend` 只推荐 approved candidates；`hold` 展示已检索的候选资料与文献结果，说明缺口和验证计划，不推荐或排序候选。

## 候选方案纪律

- 候选配方必须来自 KG 结构化证据或文献 chunk；
- 对于"建议组合"（无完整配方直接实验数据），summary 只写组分和证据来源，不写性能声明；
- 性能/效果声明只能绑定到直接支持该声明的 chunk_id；
- 禁止在"证据摘要"里写入未被任何 chunk 直接支持的推断句；无来源支撑的直接删除；
- **直接回答（direct_answer）只给出候选方案标识和最精简组成**，不要包含"已在某温度验证"、"性能最优"、"最有效"等需要跨证据推断的断言；
- 推荐完整配方必须有原文明确的钠盐浓度。若浓度未知，列为待补资料，不得填入
  “参考基准配方”的浓度并作为已有文献验证的配方推荐。

## 推荐/排序纪律

- 排序理由必须逐条绑定到具体 chunk_id，禁止写"C1/C3/C4 无法满足需求"、"某候选明显优于其他"等无直接对比证据的绝对化断言；
- 无直接对比证据时，只陈述各候选的组分、证据来源与评分，不给出相对优劣结论；
- 对"建议组合"的推荐，只能说明其组分和所依据的证据，不得把多篇证据的性能迁移到该组合上。

## 证据摘要纪律

- 配方段落若讨论多种浓度、多个溶剂比例或不同研究，先定位到单一配方的原文。
  不得把某段的浓度、另一配方的溶剂比例和第三个体系的添加剂拼成候选。
  原文工具返回中的数值、温度符号、配方标识和 chunk_id 应原样沿用，
  不得手工改写成另一温度或用整篇论文的共同身份代替相同测试条件。
- 每条 bullet 必须附带 `[chunk_id]`；
- 禁止输出以"【推断】"开头的句子；
- 禁止把多篇证据的性能迁移到某个候选配方上。

## 引用纪律

- 使用 `[chunk_id]` 格式；
- 禁止引用模型参数知识里的文献；
- 单篇报道就写"某文献报道/某体系显示"，不得升格为普适结论。

## KG 质量反馈

检索或分析过程中，若发现以下可疑情况，**必须**调用 `flag_suspicious_kg_item` 记录，供后续离线人工审查与 KG 矫正；不阻塞当前设计流程。

- **实体标签错误**：如 `ionic conductivity` 被标为 `Additive`，`NaPF6` 被标为 `Solvent`；
- **关系方向/语义错误**：如 `SEI DECOMPOSITION::FORMS::FEC`、明显违背化学常识的关系；
- **属性单位或数值异常**：如电导率 `100 mS/cm` 与上下文矛盾、温度单位混用；
- **同名异义**：如 `TMP` 同时指 `trimethyl phosphate` 与 `2,4,6-trimethylpyridine` 而未区分；
- **证据与 KG 矛盾**：chunk 中的明确结论与 KG 检索结果冲突。

记录时尽量提供：item_type（`entity`/`relation`/`property`）、具体名称/ID、问题描述、触发工具、证据 chunk_id。

供下次相似问题时直接检索复用，减少重复检索成本。

In summary, a commercially feasible sodium-ion pouch cell with $Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ /hard carbon is fabricated in this work. According to the calculation of the frontier molecular orbital energy, the electrolyte additive adiponitrile (ADN) is selected as the electrolyte additive to improve the performance of sodium-ion battery for the first time, and the effects of the ADN on the performance improvement of the cathode material $Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ are investigated for the first time. The results show that ADN can promote the formation of highly conductive and stable SEI film on the cathode material surface, and effectively improve the high-low-temperature performance and cycling stability of $Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ as the cathode electrode material of sodium-ion batteries. In particular, the battery with 3% ADN shows the most obvious improvement, its discharge capacity increases by 10.5%, 8%, and 13% at the operating temperature of 45, -10, and -20 °C, respectively. RESULTS AND DISCUSSION
Low-temperature cyclability is one of the key advantages of sodium-ion batteries. However, reduced kinetics at low temperatures hinder the efficient intercalation of sodium ions into hard carbon, leading to metallic sodium deposition on electrode surfaces, which results in capacity degradation and safety concerns. To address this issue, we investigated the effects of the PFPN additive on low-temperature performance using a 0.4 Ah-level NFM-HC pouch cell. The cells underwent a formation process at a 0.1 C rate, as shown in the formation curves in Figure S1. The charge and discharge curves of both cells were nearly identical. Subsequent EIS analysis after formation revealed that cells with the electrolyte containing 10 wt % PFPN exhibited lower resistance (Figure 1a), indicating that the PFPN additive effectively reduces interfacial resistance in the cells.

The low-temperature cyclability of cells with the baseline electrolyte and 10 wt % PFPN additive was evaluated at 0 °C and 0.2 C rate (Figure 1b–d). Notably, the cell with 10 wt % PFPN additive demonstrated approximately 4% higher capacity retention compared to the baseline electrolyte (81.33%) after 450 cycles (Figure 1b). During cycling, the average Coulombic efficiency of the baseline electrolyte was 99.939%, whereas the electrolyte containing 10 wt % PFPN achieved 99.951%. Although the charge–discharge curves (Figure 1c) did not immediately reveal significant differences between the electrolytes, the differential voltage curves (Figure S2) highlighted distinct behaviors. The baseline electrolyte exhibited a larger capacity loss in the adsorption–desorption region of the hard carbon anode after cycling (shown in the red area), indicating a reduction in effective adsorption sites on the electrode surface. $^{31}$ Interestingly, we discovered that the PFPN additive effectively suppressed these polarization deteriorations throughout the cycling process. evidence.text: To evaluate the electrochemical performance of the electrolyte, Na+ HC cells were assembled. As shown in Fig. 3a, CIE provides a specific capacity of 300.5 mAh g-1 and an initial Coulombic efficiency (ICE) of 93.7% during the first cycle at 25°C, while CCE and WSE provide specific capacities of 299.6 and 300.1 mAh g-1 and ICE of 87.7% and 91.4%, respectively.

evidence.text: The voltage ranges of Na||HC cells and HC||NFM pouch batteries were 0 to 2.5 V and 1.8 to 3.8 V, respectively. For pouch cells, cycle at 50 mA for 2 h, followed by 100 mA for 1 h, then 200 mA for 2.5 h. After a 36 h rest period, charge at 200 mA until full capacity is reached, then discharge to 1.8 V to complete the activation process. The entire procedure is conducted at 45 °C.

candidates.rationale: 0125 Byun 等 硬碳/O3 层状氧化物软包电池用 LiPF6 添加电解液：1.0 M NaPF6 EC/DMC=1:1 v/v + 0.5 wt% FEC + 0.2 M LiPF6；软包电池库仑效率改善、400 循环保持 92.7%（室温条件）。

evidence.paper_title: Transformative Effect of Li Salt for Practical Sodium-Ion Pouch Cells (hard carbon / O3-type layered oxide)
evidence.text: 0.5 wt% FEC (Soulbrain), 0.2 M LiPF6 (Chunbo), and 0.2 M lithium difluoro(oxalato)borate (LiODFB) were added to 1.0 M NaPF6 EC/DMC (1:1 = v/v, Dongwha Electrolyte), respectively. This mixture was prepared in an Ar-filled glove box and stirred overnight.

evidence.chunk_id: 0125_0141_Transformative_Effect_of_Li_Salt_for_Pro::sec13
evidence.paper_id: 0125_0141_Transformative_Effect_of_Li_Salt_for_Pro
evidence.paper_title: Transformative Effect of Li Salt for Practical Sodium-Ion Pouch Cells (hard carbon / O3-type layered oxide)
evidence.text: LiPF6 additive was incorporated in the pouch cell composed of the hard carbon/O3-type positive electrode and evaluated (Fig. 4a). The addition of the LiPF6 salt in the electrolyte improved capacity retention considerably compared with that of the typical FEC-added electrolyte. While the FEC-added pouch cell exhibited a capacity retention of 73.1% at the 400th cycle, the addition of LiPF6 salt in the SIB electrolyte demonstrated a capacity retention of 92.7% at the same cycle number. ... The improved Coulombic efficiency was observed at pouch cell with LiPF6-added electrolyte than that of FEC-added electrolyte-injected cell (Fig. S8).

evidence.text: Before electrochemical characterization, the pouch cell was rested for 24 h at room temperature. The pouch cell formation was performed with a CC-CV charge of 0.1 C (with a 0.05 C cutoff) and with a CC discharge of 0.1 C, over a voltage range of 2.5–4.0 V.

evidence_chunks.content:
The main raw materials used for preparing functional electrolytes, including EC, EMC, $NaPF_{6}$ , NaDFP, TMSP and TMSB were provided by the Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co, Ltd. The baseline electrolyte was prepared by dissolving $NaPF_{6}$ in a mixture of EC: EMC=3:7 to form a concentration of 0.8 mol $L^{-1}$ . Then, NaDFP was added into the baseline electrolyte to prepare the NaDFP electrolyte, and NaDFP and

TMSB or TMSP were respectively added into the baseline electrolyte and assigned as NB or NP electrolyte. All electrolytes were prepared in a dry argon filled glove box with both moisture and oxygen concentrations below 0.1 ppm. NFM was purchased from Jiangsu Xiangying New Energy Technology Co, Ltd, HC was purchased from Kuraray Co Ltd. The pouch test cells with NFM cathode (120 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 0.1 C), HC anode (290 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 0.05 C), and Celgard 2700 separator were assembled using the conventional assembly method. Therein, NFM active material, polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF), carbon nanotube (CNT), conductive carbon black (Super P), and Maleic acid (the reason of addition maleic acid was shown in Table 1) were dispersed in N-methylpyrrolidone (NMP) with a mass ratio of 94.5:1.8:1:2.5:0.2, and the slurry was coated on an aluminum substrate to prepare the NFM cathode.

evidence_chunks.content: The coulombic efficiencies of the first cycle for diverse pouch NFM/HC SIBs were different, as shown in Fig. 3h, which also confirm that film-forming process was changed after the addition of different additives. Based on these results, it can be concluded that benefited by the optimized solvation structure with lower desolvation energy and superior physical properties, NB and NP electrolytes can be expected to induce enhanced performance of SIBs at tough temperature conditions than the baseline and NaDFP-containing electrolytes.

evidence_chunks.content: With the help of "hard-soft synergy", polarization and capacity fading are alleviated signally during the cycling. Besides, rate performance of pouch cells is also improved by the synergistic effect of NP or NB electrolyte even at $-10^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ and $1\mathrm{C}$ , as shown in Fig. 4d and S5b. Furthermore, to evaluate dual additive potential at tougher low-temperatures, $-20^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ and $-30^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ discharge tests are necessary. Fig. 4e shows the capacity retention of pouch cells at different discharge currents, revealing the cells all can exhibit good electrochemical performance under the tested temperature conditions. Even at $-30^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ and $1\mathrm{C}$ , the discharge capacity of pouch cells with NP and NB electrolytes still achieves $729\mathrm{mAh}$ and $697\mathrm{mAh}$ , respectively. These results confirm that this co-additive addition strategy improves extremely low temperature performance of NFM/HC pouch cells. Summarily, compared to single additive or baseline electrolyte, NFM/HC pouch cells with multi-component functional electrolyte possess much better performance. Therein, the cells containing NP electrolyte have better room and high-temperature performance, and the cells containing NB electrolyte are more suitable for low-temperature application.

source_refs.raw_quote:
The main raw materials used for preparing functional electrolytes, including EC, EMC, $NaPF_{6}$ , NaDFP, TMSP and TMSB were provided by the Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co, Ltd. The baseline electrolyte was prepared by dissolving $NaPF_{6}$ in a mixture of EC: EMC=3:7 to form a concentration of 0.8 mol $L^{-1}$ . Then, NaDFP was added into the baseline electrolyte to prepare the NaDFP electrolyte, and NaDFP and

TMSB or TMSP were respectively added into the baseline electrolyte and assigned as NB or NP electrolyte. All electrolytes were prepared in a dry argon filled glove box with both moisture and oxygen concentrations below 0.1 ppm. NFM was purchased from Jiangsu Xiangying New Energy Technology Co, Ltd, HC was purchased from Kuraray Co Ltd. The pouch test cells with NFM cathode (120 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 0.1 C), HC anode (290 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 0.05 C), and Celgard 2700 separator were assembled using the conventional assembly method. Therein, NFM active material, polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF), carbon nanotube (CNT), conductive carbon black (Super P), and Maleic acid (the reason of addition maleic acid was shown in Table 1) were dispersed in N-methylpyrrolidone (NMP) with a mass ratio of 94.5:1.8:1:2.5:0.2, and the slurry was coated on an aluminum substrate to prepare the NFM cathode.

source_refs.raw_quote: The coulombic efficiencies of the first cycle for diverse pouch NFM/HC SIBs were different, as shown in Fig. 3h, which also confirm that film-forming process was changed after the addition of different additives. Based on these results, it can be concluded that benefited by the optimized solvation structure with lower desolvation energy and superior physical properties, NB and NP electrolytes can be expected to induce enhanced performance of SIBs at tough temperature conditions than the baseline and NaDFP-containing electrolytes.

source_refs.raw_quote: With the help of "hard-soft synergy", polarization and capacity fading are alleviated signally during the cycling. Besides, rate performance of pouch cells is also improved by the synergistic effect of NP or NB electrolyte even at $-10^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ and $1\mathrm{C}$ , as shown in Fig. 4d and S5b. Furthermore, to evaluate dual additive potential at tougher low-temperatures, $-20^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ and $-30^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ discharge tests are necessary. Fig. 4e shows the capacity retention of pouch cells at different discharge currents, revealing the cells all can exhibit good electrochemical performance under the tested temperature conditions. Even at $-30^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ and $1\mathrm{C}$ , the discharge capacity of pouch cells with NP and NB electrolytes still achieves $729\mathrm{mAh}$ and $697\mathrm{mAh}$ , respectively. These results confirm that this co-additive addition strategy improves extremely low temperature performance of NFM/HC pouch cells. Summarily, compared to single additive or baseline electrolyte, NFM/HC pouch cells with multi-component functional electrolyte possess much better performance. Therein, the cells containing NP electrolyte have better room and high-temperature performance, and the cells containing NB electrolyte are more suitable for low-temperature application.

source_refs.raw_quote: In summary, a commercially feasible sodium-ion pouch cell with $Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ /hard carbon is fabricated in this work. According to the calculation of the frontier molecular orbital energy, the electrolyte additive adiponitrile (ADN) is selected as the electrolyte additive to improve the performance of sodium-ion battery for the first time, and the effects of the ADN on the performance improvement of the cathode material $Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ are investigated for the first time. The results show that ADN can promote the formation of highly conductive and stable SEI film on the cathode material surface, and effectively improve the high-low-temperature performance and cycling stability of $Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ as the cathode electrode material of sodium-ion batteries. In particular, the battery with 3% ADN shows the most obvious improvement, its discharge capacity increases by 10.5%, 8%, and 13% at the operating temperature of 45, -10, and -20 °C, respectively. For the cycling stability, the capacity retention rate of the battery without adding ADN drops rapidly to 75% after 40 cycles, while the capacity retention rate of the battery with 3% ADN can still reach 78% after 220 cycles. Adding ADN as electrolyte additive effectively improves the electrochemical performance of sodium ion batteries.

source_refs.raw_quote: $Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ , carbon nanotubes (CNTs), polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF), and carbon black with the mass ratio of 92.5: 2.0: 3.5: 2.0 were mixed in pyrrolidone to form a uniform slurry, and then coated on a 14 um thick aluminum foil to prepare the cathode electrode. The areal density was measured to be 10.0 mg cm $^{-2}$ , and the compacted density was 2.1 g cm $^{-3}$ . To prepare the anode electrode, hard carbon (Kuraray), carbon black, cellulose sodium (CMC), and styrene butadiene rubber (SBR) with the mass ratio of 94.5: 1.0: 2.0: 2.5 were added in deionized water and stirred into a uniform slurry, and then coated on a 9 um thick copper foil with the areal and compacted densities of 4.31 mg cm $^{-2}$ and 1.4 g cm $^{-3}$ , respectively. The cathode, anode, and separator (20 μm polypropylene) were assembled into pouch cells with a designed capacity of 650 mAh, and the thickness, width, and length were 10, 68, and 127 mm, respectively. The cells were dried in vacuum (-99 kPa/80 °C) until the water content was less than 150 ppm. At a dewpoint of -40 °C, the electrolytes defined as G1, G2, G3, and G4 (Table 1) were injected into the cells. After packaging in vacuum at room temperature for 48 hours; the pouch cells were placed at the environment with 0.8 MPa and 45 °C and charged at 0.05 C for 180 min, followed by another charge at a constant current of 0.1 C for 360 min.

source_refs.raw_quote: The sodium hexafluorophosphate (NaPF $_6$ , 99.8% min), diethylene glycol dimethyl ether (G2, 99.8% min) and 2-methyloxolane (MO, 99.8% min) were purchased from DoDo Chem. Common ether electrolyte (CCE) was prepared by dissolving 0.8 M NaPF $_6$ in G2 solvent. Weakly solvated electrolyte (WSE) was prepared by dissolving 0.8 M NaPF $_6$ in MO solvent. Co-intercalated electrolyte (CIE) was prepared by dissolving 0.8 M NaPF $_6$ in G2: MO = 7:3 vol%. All electrolyte preparation processes were carried out in a glovebox filled with Ar (H $_2$ O < 0.1 ppm and O $_2$ < 0.1 ppm). The electrolyte salts and solvents we purchased are of anhydrous grade. After purchase, they are placed in the glove box for direct use. Hard carbon (HC) materials were purchased from Baisige New Energy Co., Ltd. The HC negative electrode was prepared by mixing the active material, CMC (CMC2200, purchased from Daicel Corporation), SBR (BM-451B, purchased from Zeon Corporation) and conductive carbon black (weight ratio 92:1.5:3.5:3) in deionized water to form a homogeneous slurry. The slurry was spread on a copper foil (thickness 18 $\mu$ m) and dried at 80 °C for 8–12 h. Then, it was perforated into a circular electrode sheet with a diameter of 12 mm and a loading of 2.5–3.0 mg cm $^{-2}$ . Glass fiber (GF/D, Whatman) was used as separator and metallic sodium (purchased from Canrd Technology Co. Ltd.) was used as counter electrode.

source_refs.raw_quote: To verify the practical applicability of CIE, we assembled a 1.2 Ah (163 Wh kg $^{-1}$ ) pouch cell with O3-type NFM positive electrode and HC negative electrode (Fig. 6a). Figure 6b shows the cycling performance of the pouch cell at different temperatures. At 25 °C, the pouch cell provides a capacity of 1.18 Ah. As the temperature decreases, we verify the possibility of its operation at low temperatures, at -50 °C, the pouch cell still provides a capacity of 0.79 Ah (107 Wh kg $^{-1}$ ), demonstrating a significantly better low-temperature adaptability than that of conventional electrolytes. Moreover, even at -50 °C, the charge/discharge curve maintains a stable voltage plateau (Fig. 6c). Figure 6d shows the cycling performance of the pouch cell at -20 °C with 94.1% capacity retention after 300 cycles. In addition, in order to visually verify the practical application potential, the LED lights are continuously powered at a low temperature of -50 °C. The fully-charged state pouch cells keep the LED lights working for more than 10 hours (Fig. 6e). This demonstration confirms that the CIE has good prospects for practical applications, especially at low temperatures. We further compare our results with some previously reported low-temperature sodium-ion pouch cells (Fig. 6f, Table S6) $^{26,52-58}$ , and our work is comparable to most of the advanced reported works, which fully proves that the CIE developed by us has important application value for SIBs in cold environments.

source_refs.raw_quote: To evaluate the electrochemical performance of the electrolyte, Na $^{+}$ HC cells were assembled. The structural characteristics of HC are shown in Fig. S13, and for HC, the reversible capacity during the first cycle is critical for less sodium loss. As shown in Fig. 3a, CIE provides a specific capacity of 300.5 mAh g $^{-1}$ and an initial Coulombic efficiency (ICE) of 93.7% during the first cycle at 25°C, while CCE and WSE provide specific capacities of 299.6 and 300.1 mAh g $^{-1}$ and ICE of 87.7% and 91.4%, respectively. The three electrolytes deliver similar reversible capacities, while CIE has the highest ICE. The severe electrolyte decomposition creates a thick SEI and affects ICE $^{30,31}$ , which may explain the lower ICE of CCE. For CIE and WSE, the introduction of anions enables the construction of inorganic-rich SEI, and the appropriate number of anions in CIE consumes less Na $^{+}$ during film formation, thus guaranteeing a high ICE for HC in CIE. The rate performance of HC is shown in Figure S14, where CIE still provides a specific capacity of $195.0 \, mAh g^{-1}$ at $2 \, A g^{-1}$ , while CCE and WSE maintain a specific capacity of 204.6 and $131.4 \, mAh g^{-1}$ , respectively. This phenomenon suggests that the ionic conductivity plays a crucial role in the rate performance at $25^{\circ}C$ . The CIE effectively improves the ionic conductivity while retaining the co-intercalation behavior, so the rate performance is close to that of CCE.

source_refs.raw_quote: The Na||HC half cells with various electrolytes were assembled in Ar-filled gloveboxes using 2032-type coin cells with Na metal and HC. The amount of electrolyte was controlled at $100\mu \mathrm{L}$ for each Na||HC cell. The voltage ranges of Na||HC cells and HC||NFM pouch batteries were 0 to $2.5\mathrm{V}$ and 1.8 to $3.8\mathrm{V}$ , respectively. For pouch cells, cycle at $50\mathrm{mA}$ for $2\mathrm{h}$ , followed by $100\mathrm{mA}$ for $1\mathrm{h}$ , then $200\mathrm{mA}$ for $2.5\mathrm{h}$ . After a $36\mathrm{h}$ rest period, charge at $200\mathrm{mA}$ until full capacity is reached, then discharge to $1.8\mathrm{V}$ to complete the activation process. The entire procedure is conducted at 45 °C. The Na $^{+}$ storage performance was examined in a galvanostatic charge-discharge test on NEWARE Battery Test System (BTS-610, Shenzhen, China). The ion conductivity of the electrolyte was measured at different temperatures using the CHI660D electrochemical workstation through electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) technology. Galvanostatic intermittent titration technique (GITT) testing was performed by NEWARE battery system. The test was performed in the third charge-discharge cycle at 20 mA g $^{-1}$ with a pulse time for 30 min and the intervals for 2 h. Acquire 1 data point every 5 seconds. LSV (scan rate: 10 mV s $^{-1}$ , voltage range: 2.5–5.5 V) tests were implemented by CHI660D electrochemical workstation.

source_refs.raw_quote: In practical applications, the performance of SIBs under the low-temperature conditions has attracted more attention. Similarly, based on the actual use of SIBs, the impact of different electrolytes on the low-temperature performance of SIBs was also characterized by measuring the cycle performance and rate performance at $-10^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ , as well as the rate and discharge performance at $-20^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ and $-30^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ . Similar to high-temperature performance of pouch cells, these "hard-soft synergy" functional electrolytes induce amazing low-temperature performance of NFM/HC SIBs. As shown in the Figs 4a, 4b and S5a, both pouch cells with the NB or NP electrolyte can improve the cycling performance compared to the cells with the baseline electrolyte, an excellent capacity retention of $95\%$ after 350 cycles and high stability can be obtained benefiting from the "hard-soft synergy". Notably, though the capacity of the cells with NP or NB electrolyte both over $850\mathrm{mAh}$ (NB-859 mAh vs. NP-850 mAh) after 300 cycles, the NP group shows more fluctuant coulombic efficiency than the NB group, as shown in Fig. 4b. Additionally, the charge/discharge curves of the cells with NP, NB, and baseline electrolytes are shown in Fig. 4c. With the help of "hard-soft synergy", polarization and capacity fading are alleviated signally during the cycling.

source_refs.raw_quote: Taking into account the application environment temperature and corresponding performance requirements of the SIBs, the performance parameters of pouch cells under different temperature conditions after adding different electrolytes were evaluated in a targeted manner. In order to choose the optimal concentration, part of the tough condition performance corresponding to different addition amounts of two additives is shown in Fig. S3. Considering cost and performance comprehensively, a 1:1.5 proportioning of NaDFP to TMSB or TMSB is chosen as the most suitable ratio. First, under the room and high temperatures, the emphasis of pouch cells with different electrolytes was given to the rate, cycling and storage performance parameters. The pouch cells with NB, NP, or NaDFP-containing electrolytes generally exhibit higher performance parameters than the cells with the baseline electrolyte. Under the room temperature of 25 °C, as shown in the Fig. S4a and S4b, rate and cycling performance of the pouch cells with the NB and NP-containing electrolytes is improved comparing to the cells with the baseline electrolyte, which can easily ascribed to the superior conductivity and lower desolvation energy. To further verify the effect of NP, NB, and NaDFP electrolytes at tougher conditions, rate, cycling, and storage tests at 45 °C and 60 °C were performed.

source_refs.raw_quote: In summary, “hard-soft synergy” strategy—reasonably coupling NaDFP with TMSP or TMSB as the functional electrolytes successfully achieved wide-temperature performance of pouch SIBs over a range of $-30^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ to $60^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ . Benefit to the high-quality and rich element optimized NaDFP-based CEI/SEI layers on the electrode surfaces, and optimizing electrolyte structure which decrease the desolvation energy and induce superior electrolyte properties, a high capacity retention of $92\%$ after 350 cycles and a stable cycling performance at $1\mathrm{C}$ were achieved even at $-10^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ . Besides, both the discharge capacity at $-30^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ and the capacity retention after storage at $60^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ were also greatly improved. Importantly, only tiny dose of NaDFP, TMSB/TMSP with reasonably couple could enable considerably effective performance improvement of SIBs, which is essential to reduce the cost and advance the commercialization. This work not only obtains functional electrolytes for enhanced wide-temperature performance of NFM/HC SIBs, but also sheds lights on the designing multi-functional additive electrolytes of SIBs.

Abstract: A commercially feasible sodium-ion pouch cell with a capacity of 650 mAh is fabricated using the ternary layered $\mathrm{Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_2}$ and the hard carbon as the cathode and anode materials, respectively. $1.0\mathrm{MNaPF}_6$ in the mixed carbonate solvents is served as the electrolyte. According to the calculation of the frontier molecular orbital energy, adiponitrile (ADN) has a stronger ability of electron donating than the carbonate solvents and thus is easier to be reduced on the surface of the cathode material to form the solid-electrolyte interphase (SEI) film, so ADN is selected as the electrolyte additive to improve the performance of sodium-ion battery for the first time.

2.2 Battery Assembly
$Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ , carbon nanotubes (CNTs), polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF), and carbon black with the mass ratio of 92.5: 2.0: 3.5: 2.0 were mixed in pyrrolidone to form a uniform slurry, and then coated on a 14 um thick aluminum foil to prepare the cathode electrode. The areal density was measured to be 10.0 mg cm $^{-2}$ , and the compacted density was 2.1 g cm $^{-3}$ . To prepare the anode electrode, hard carbon (Kuraray), carbon black, cellulose sodium (CMC), and styrene butadiene rubber (SBR) with the mass ratio of 94.5: 1.0: 2.0: 2.5 were added in deionized water and stirred into a uniform slurry, and then coated on a 9 um thick copper foil with the areal and compacted densities of 4.31 mg cm $^{-2}$ and 1.4 g cm $^{-3}$ , respectively. The cathode, anode, and separator (20 μm polypropylene) were assembled into pouch cells with a designed capacity of 650 mAh, and the thickness, width, and length were 10, 68, and 127 mm, respectively. The cells were dried in vacuum (-99 kPa/80 °C) until the water content was less than 150 ppm. At a dewpoint of -40 °C, the electrolytes defined as G1, G2, G3, and G4 (Table 1) were injected into the cells. After packaging in vacuum at room temperature for 48 hours; the pouch cells were placed at the environment with 0.8 MPa and 45 °C and charged at 0.05 C for 180 min, followed by another charge at a constant current of 0.1 C for 360 min. Then, the pouch cells were punctuated in vacuum to remove excess electrolyte and gas generated by the side reactions during the charge process. Eventually, the cells were packaged again and cut the air-bags to obtain the finished batteries for testing.

source_refs.raw_quote: The specific discharge capacities at different temperatures are shown in Fig. 4. At both high and low temperatures, the addition of ADN made the discharge capacity increase significantly, especially with the amount of 3%. This is because the additive ADN induces the formation of SEI film with low impedances. In particular, 3% ADN led to the formation of the SEI film with the lowest impedance and resulted in the lowest polarization. As a result, the batteries of G3 exhibited the highest discharge capacity retention rate at low temperatures. In addition, the batteries of G3 also exhibited the highest discharge capacity retention rate at high temperatures, indicating that the SEI film formed from the induction of ADN has a better stability at high temperatures. On the contrary, the discharge capacity retention rates of the batteries of G1 are the lowest at both high and low temperatures, demonstrating that the SEI film formed by the electrolyte without the additive ADN has large impedance and poor stability at high temperatures. To further understand the different rate and low-temperature performance of the batteries with different volume of electrolyte additive, the electrochemical impedance of each battery was tested (Fig. 5D). The electrochemical impedance spectra of the batteries of G1, G2, G3, and G4 showed flat semicircles in the high-frequency regions.

source_refs.raw_quote: To solve this problem, a CIE was designed in this work. The design principle is based on the following findings: there are always some solvents in the electrolyte that do not participate in the coordination and only act as ion transport media, which are called free solvents. For this reason, we replaced this part of free solvent with 2-methyloxolane (MO) which has a lower melting point ( $-136^{\circ}C$ , Table S1) and is less polar. Through this strategy, not only the co-embeddable solvation structure is retained and the ion transport kinetics are accelerated, but also the working temperature range of electrolyte in low-temperature environment is significantly widened by increasing the solvation entropy. To highlight the progressiveness of our designed electrolyte, we also used common co-intercalation ether electrolyte (CCE) and WSE as controls, and the specific electrolyte formulation is shown in Table S2. According to the optical photographs in Figure S1, CCE starts to have salt precipitation at $-30^{\circ}C$ , and it is even completely solidified at $-50^{\circ}C$ . On the other hand, WSE and our CIE remain liquid at $-50^{\circ}C$ , which effectively guarantees the possibility of electrolyte application at low temperatures. The ion transport mechanisms of various electrolytes at low temperatures are shown in Fig. 1, among which the CIE has the fastest ion transport rate due to the presence of the co-intercalation behavior.

citations.quote:
The main raw materials used for preparing functional electrolytes, including EC, EMC, $NaPF_{6}$ , NaDFP, TMSP and TMSB were provided by the Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co, Ltd. The baseline electrolyte was prepared by dissolving $NaPF_{6}$ in a mixture of EC: EMC=3:7 to form a concentration of 0.8 mol $L^{-1}$ . Then, NaDFP was added into the baseline electrolyte to prepare the NaDFP electrolyte, and NaDFP and

TMSB or TMSP were respectively added into the baseline electrolyte and assigned as NB or NP electrolyte. All electrolytes were prepared in a dry argon filled glove box with both moisture and oxygen concentrations below 0.1 ppm. NFM was purchased from Jiangsu Xiangying New Energy Technology Co, Ltd, HC was purchased from Kuraray Co Ltd. The pouch test cells with NFM cathode (120 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 0.1 C), HC anode (290 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 0.05 C), and Celgard 2700 separator were assembled using the conventional assembly method. Therein, NFM active material, polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF), carbon nanotube (CNT), conductive carbon black (Super P), and Maleic acid (the reason of addition maleic acid was shown in Table 1) were dispersed in N-methylpyrrolidone (NMP) with a mass ratio of 94.5:1.8:1:2.5:0.2, and the slurry was coated on an aluminum substrate to prepare the NFM cathode.

citations.chunk_id: 0156_Cai 等 - 2025 - A hard-soft synergy strategy enables drastic temperature performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries o::sec8::child2
citations.quote: In practical applications, the performance of SIBs under the low-temperature conditions has attracted more attention. Similarly, based on the actual use of SIBs, the impact of different electrolytes on the low-temperature performance of SIBs was also characterized by measuring the cycle performance and rate performance at $-10^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ , as well as the rate and discharge performance at $-20^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ and $-30^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ . Similar to high-temperature performance of pouch cells, these "hard-soft synergy" functional electrolytes induce amazing low-temperature performance of NFM/HC SIBs. As shown in the Figs 4a, 4b and S5a, both pouch cells with the NB or NP electrolyte can improve the cycling performance compared to the cells with the baseline electrolyte, an excellent capacity retention of $95\%$ after 350 cycles and high stability can be obtained benefiting from the "hard-soft synergy". Notably, though the capacity of the cells with NP or NB electrolyte both over $850\mathrm{mAh}$ (NB-859 mAh vs. NP-850 mAh) after 300 cycles, the NP group shows more fluctuant coulombic efficiency than the NB group, as shown in Fig. 4b. Additionally, the charge/discharge curves of the cells with NP, NB, and baseline electrolytes are shown in Fig. 4c. With the help of "hard-soft synergy", polarization and capacity fading are alleviated signally during the cycling.

citations.chunk_id: 0156_Cai 等 - 2025 - A hard-soft synergy strategy enables drastic temperature performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries o::sec8::child0
citations.quote: Taking into account the application environment temperature and corresponding performance requirements of the SIBs, the performance parameters of pouch cells under different temperature conditions after adding different electrolytes were evaluated in a targeted manner. In order to choose the optimal concentration, part of the tough condition performance corresponding to different addition amounts of two additives is shown in Fig. S3. Considering cost and performance comprehensively, a 1:1.5 proportioning of NaDFP to TMSB or TMSB is chosen as the most suitable ratio. First, under the room and high temperatures, the emphasis of pouch cells with different electrolytes was given to the rate, cycling and storage performance parameters. The pouch cells with NB, NP, or NaDFP-containing electrolytes generally exhibit higher performance parameters than the cells with the baseline electrolyte. Under the room temperature of 25 °C, as shown in the Fig. S4a and S4b, rate and cycling performance of the pouch cells with the NB and NP-containing electrolytes is improved comparing to the cells with the baseline electrolyte, which can easily ascribed to the superior conductivity and lower desolvation energy. To further verify the effect of NP, NB, and NaDFP electrolytes at tougher conditions, rate, cycling, and storage tests at 45 °C and 60 °C were performed.

citations.chunk_id: 0156_Cai 等 - 2025 - A hard-soft synergy strategy enables drastic temperature performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries o::sec8::child3
citations.quote: With the help of "hard-soft synergy", polarization and capacity fading are alleviated signally during the cycling. Besides, rate performance of pouch cells is also improved by the synergistic effect of NP or NB electrolyte even at $-10^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ and $1\mathrm{C}$ , as shown in Fig. 4d and S5b. Furthermore, to evaluate dual additive potential at tougher low-temperatures, $-20^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ and $-30^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ discharge tests are necessary. Fig. 4e shows the capacity retention of pouch cells at different discharge currents, revealing the cells all can exhibit good electrochemical performance under the tested temperature conditions. Even at $-30^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ and $1\mathrm{C}$ , the discharge capacity of pouch cells with NP and NB electrolytes still achieves $729\mathrm{mAh}$ and $697\mathrm{mAh}$ , respectively. These results confirm that this co-additive addition strategy improves extremely low temperature performance of NFM/HC pouch cells. Summarily, compared to single additive or baseline electrolyte, NFM/HC pouch cells with multi-component functional electrolyte possess much better performance. Therein, the cells containing NP electrolyte have better room and high-temperature performance, and the cells containing NB electrolyte are more suitable for low-temperature application.

citations.chunk_id: 0156_Cai 等 - 2025 - A hard-soft synergy strategy enables drastic temperature performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries o::sec10::child0
citations.quote: In summary, “hard-soft synergy” strategy—reasonably coupling NaDFP with TMSP or TMSB as the functional electrolytes successfully achieved wide-temperature performance of pouch SIBs over a range of $-30^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ to $60^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ . Benefit to the high-quality and rich element optimized NaDFP-based CEI/SEI layers on the electrode surfaces, and optimizing electrolyte structure which decrease the desolvation energy and induce superior electrolyte properties, a high capacity retention of $92\%$ after 350 cycles and a stable cycling performance at $1\mathrm{C}$ were achieved even at $-10^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ . Besides, both the discharge capacity at $-30^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ and the capacity retention after storage at $60^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ were also greatly improved. Importantly, only tiny dose of NaDFP, TMSB/TMSP with reasonably couple could enable considerably effective performance improvement of SIBs, which is essential to reduce the cost and advance the commercialization. This work not only obtains functional electrolytes for enhanced wide-temperature performance of NFM/HC SIBs, but also sheds lights on the designing multi-functional additive electrolytes of SIBs.

Abstract: A commercially feasible sodium-ion pouch cell with a capacity of 650 mAh is fabricated using the ternary layered $\mathrm{Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_2}$ and the hard carbon as the cathode and anode materials, respectively. $1.0\mathrm{MNaPF}_6$ in the mixed carbonate solvents is served as the electrolyte. According to the calculation of the frontier molecular orbital energy, adiponitrile (ADN) has a stronger ability of electron donating than the carbonate solvents and thus is easier to be reduced on the surface of the cathode material to form the solid-electrolyte interphase (SEI) film, so ADN is selected as the electrolyte additive to improve the performance of sodium-ion battery for the first time.

2.2 Battery Assembly
$Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ , carbon nanotubes (CNTs), polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF), and carbon black with the mass ratio of 92.5: 2.0: 3.5: 2.0 were mixed in pyrrolidone to form a uniform slurry, and then coated on a 14 um thick aluminum foil to prepare the cathode electrode. The areal density was measured to be 10.0 mg cm $^{-2}$ , and the compacted density was 2.1 g cm $^{-3}$ . To prepare the anode electrode, hard carbon (Kuraray), carbon black, cellulose sodium (CMC), and styrene butadiene rubber (SBR) with the mass ratio of 94.5: 1.0: 2.0: 2.5 were added in deionized water and stirred into a uniform slurry, and then coated on a 9 um thick copper foil with the areal and compacted densities of 4.31 mg cm $^{-2}$ and 1.4 g cm $^{-3}$ , respectively. The cathode, anode, and separator (20 μm polypropylene) were assembled into pouch cells with a designed capacity of 650 mAh, and the thickness, width, and length were 10, 68, and 127 mm, respectively. The cells were dried in vacuum (-99 kPa/80 °C) until the water content was less than 150 ppm. At a dewpoint of -40 °C, the electrolytes defined as G1, G2, G3, and G4 (Table 1) were injected into the cells. After packaging in vacuum at room temperature for 48 hours; the pouch cells were placed at the environment with 0.8 MPa and 45 °C and charged at 0.05 C for 180 min, followed by another charge at a constant current of 0.1 C for 360 min. Then, the pouch cells were punctuated in vacuum to remove excess electrolyte and gas generated by the side reactions during the charge process. Eventually, the cells were packaged again and cut the air-bags to obtain the finished batteries for testing.

citations.quote: In summary, a commercially feasible sodium-ion pouch cell with $Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ /hard carbon is fabricated in this work. According to the calculation of the frontier molecular orbital energy, the electrolyte additive adiponitrile (ADN) is selected as the electrolyte additive to improve the performance of sodium-ion battery for the first time, and the effects of the ADN on the performance improvement of the cathode material $Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ are investigated for the first time. The results show that ADN can promote the formation of highly conductive and stable SEI film on the cathode material surface, and effectively improve the high-low-temperature performance and cycling stability of $Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ as the cathode electrode material of sodium-ion batteries. In particular, the battery with 3% ADN shows the most obvious improvement, its discharge capacity increases by 10.5%, 8%, and 13% at the operating temperature of 45, -10, and -20 °C, respectively. For the cycling stability, the capacity retention rate of the battery without adding ADN drops rapidly to 75% after 40 cycles, while the capacity retention rate of the battery with 3% ADN can still reach 78% after 220 cycles. Adding ADN as electrolyte additive effectively improves the electrochemical performance of sodium ion batteries.

citations.chunk_id: 0061_Song 等 - 2018 - The effects of the functional electrolyte additive on the cathode material Na076Ni03Fe04Mn03O2 f::sec7::child4
citations.quote: The specific discharge capacities at different temperatures are shown in Fig. 4. At both high and low temperatures, the addition of ADN made the discharge capacity increase significantly, especially with the amount of 3%. This is because the additive ADN induces the formation of SEI film with low impedances. In particular, 3% ADN led to the formation of the SEI film with the lowest impedance and resulted in the lowest polarization. As a result, the batteries of G3 exhibited the highest discharge capacity retention rate at low temperatures. In addition, the batteries of G3 also exhibited the highest discharge capacity retention rate at high temperatures, indicating that the SEI film formed from the induction of ADN has a better stability at high temperatures. On the contrary, the discharge capacity retention rates of the batteries of G1 are the lowest at both high and low temperatures, demonstrating that the SEI film formed by the electrolyte without the additive ADN has large impedance and poor stability at high temperatures. To further understand the different rate and low-temperature performance of the batteries with different volume of electrolyte additive, the electrochemical impedance of each battery was tested (Fig. 5D). The electrochemical impedance spectra of the batteries of G1, G2, G3, and G4 showed flat semicircles in the high-frequency regions.

citations.quote: The sodium hexafluorophosphate (NaPF $_6$ , 99.8% min), diethylene glycol dimethyl ether (G2, 99.8% min) and 2-methyloxolane (MO, 99.8% min) were purchased from DoDo Chem. Common ether electrolyte (CCE) was prepared by dissolving 0.8 M NaPF $_6$ in G2 solvent. Weakly solvated electrolyte (WSE) was prepared by dissolving 0.8 M NaPF $_6$ in MO solvent. Co-intercalated electrolyte (CIE) was prepared by dissolving 0.8 M NaPF $_6$ in G2: MO = 7:3 vol%. All electrolyte preparation processes were carried out in a glovebox filled with Ar (H $_2$ O < 0.1 ppm and O $_2$ < 0.1 ppm). The electrolyte salts and solvents we purchased are of anhydrous grade. After purchase, they are placed in the glove box for direct use. Hard carbon (HC) materials were purchased from Baisige New Energy Co., Ltd. The HC negative electrode was prepared by mixing the active material, CMC (CMC2200, purchased from Daicel Corporation), SBR (BM-451B, purchased from Zeon Corporation) and conductive carbon black (weight ratio 92:1.5:3.5:3) in deionized water to form a homogeneous slurry. The slurry was spread on a copper foil (thickness 18 $\mu$ m) and dried at 80 °C for 8–12 h. citations.quote: To solve this problem, a CIE was designed in this work. The design principle is based on the following findings: there are always some solvents in the electrolyte that do not participate in the coordination and only act as ion transport media, which are called free solvents. For this reason, we replaced this part of free solvent with 2-methyloxolane (MO) which has a lower melting point ( $-136^{\circ}C$ , Table S1) and is less polar. Through this strategy, not only the co-embeddable solvation structure is retained and the ion transport kinetics are accelerated, but also the working temperature range of electrolyte in low-temperature environment is significantly widened by increasing the solvation entropy. To highlight the progressiveness of our designed electrolyte, we also used common co-intercalation ether electrolyte (CCE) and WSE as controls, and the specific electrolyte formulation is shown in Table S2. According to the optical photographs in Figure S1, CCE starts to have salt precipitation at $-30^{\circ}C$ , and it is even completely solidified at $-50^{\circ}C$ . On the other hand, WSE and our CIE remain liquid at $-50^{\circ}C$ , which effectively guarantees the possibility of electrolyte application at low temperatures. The ion transport mechanisms of various electrolytes at low temperatures are shown in Fig. 1, among which the CIE has the fastest ion transport rate due to the presence of the co-intercalation behavior.

citations.quote: To verify the practical applicability of CIE, we assembled a 1.2 Ah (163 Wh kg $^{-1}$ ) pouch cell with O3-type NFM positive electrode and HC negative electrode (Fig. 6a). Figure 6b shows the cycling performance of the pouch cell at different temperatures. At 25 °C, the pouch cell provides a capacity of 1.18 Ah. As the temperature decreases, we verify the possibility of its operation at low temperatures, at -50 °C, the pouch cell still provides a capacity of 0.79 Ah (107 Wh kg $^{-1}$ ), demonstrating a significantly better low-temperature adaptability than that of conventional electrolytes. Moreover, even at -50 °C, the charge/discharge curve maintains a stable voltage plateau (Fig. 6c). Figure 6d shows the cycling performance of the pouch cell at -20 °C with 94.1% capacity retention after 300 cycles. In addition, in order to visually verify the practical application potential, the LED lights are continuously powered at a low temperature of -50 °C. The fully-charged state pouch cells keep the LED lights working for more than 10 hours (Fig. 6e). This demonstration confirms that the CIE has good prospects for practical applications, especially at low temperatures. We further compare our results with some previously reported low-temperature sodium-ion pouch cells (Fig. 6f, Table S6) $^{26,52-58}$ , and our work is comparable to most of the advanced reported works, which fully proves that the CIE developed by us has important application value for SIBs in cold environments.

citations.quote: To evaluate the electrochemical performance of the electrolyte, Na $^{+}$ HC cells were assembled. The structural characteristics of HC are shown in Fig. S13, and for HC, the reversible capacity during the first cycle is critical for less sodium loss. As shown in Fig. 3a, CIE provides a specific capacity of 300.5 mAh g $^{-1}$ and an initial Coulombic efficiency (ICE) of 93.7% during the first cycle at 25°C, while CCE and WSE provide specific capacities of 299.6 and 300.1 mAh g $^{-1}$ and ICE of 87.7% and 91.4%, respectively. The three electrolytes deliver similar reversible capacities, while CIE has the highest ICE. The severe electrolyte decomposition creates a thick SEI and affects ICE $^{30,31}$ , which may explain the lower ICE of CCE. For CIE and WSE, the introduction of anions enables the construction of inorganic-rich SEI, and the appropriate number of anions in CIE consumes less Na $^{+}$ during film formation, thus guaranteeing a high ICE for HC in CIE. The rate performance of HC is shown in Figure S14, where CIE still provides a specific capacity of $195.0 \, mAh g^{-1}$ at $2 \, A g^{-1}$ , while CCE and WSE maintain a specific capacity of 204.6 and $131.4 \, mAh g^{-1}$ , respectively. This phenomenon suggests that the ionic conductivity plays a crucial role in the rate performance at $25^{\circ}C$ . The CIE effectively improves the ionic conductivity while retaining the co-intercalation behavior, so the rate performance is close to that of CCE.

citations.quote: $\mathrm{LiPF_6}$ additive was incorporated in the pouch cell composed of the hard carbon/O3-type positive electrode and evaluated (Fig. 4a). The addition of the $\mathrm{LiPF_6}$ salt in the electrolyte improved capacity retention considerably compared with that of the typical FEC-added electrolyte. While the FEC-added pouch cell exhibited a capacity retention of $73.1\%$ at the 400th cycle, the addition of $\mathrm{LiPF_6}$ salt in the SIB electrolyte demonstrated a capacity retention of $92.7\%$ at the same cycle number. This achieved capacity retention is highly surpasses previously reported results, which is typically about $80\%$ (Table S1). The working nominal voltage change during the cycle indicates that the development of polarization from side reactions occurred in the case of the FEC-added cell (Fig. 4b). The working voltage with the $LiPF_{6}$ -added electrolyte was highly preserved in different cycles, implying that the energy delivered from the addition of the $LiPF_{6}$ pouch cell was well retained after the 400th cycle. Figure 4b demonstrates the cycle number-dependent voltage profiles obtained from hard carbon/O3-type positive electrode pouch cells. While polarization increased during repeated cycling in the FEC-added cell case, the $LiPF_{6}$ -added cell showed a stable voltage profile even after the 400th cycle.

The main raw materials used for preparing functional electrolytes, including EC, EMC, $NaPF_{6}$ , NaDFP, TMSP and TMSB were provided by the Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co, Ltd. The baseline electrolyte was prepared by dissolving $NaPF_{6}$ in a mixture of EC: EMC=3:7 to form a concentration of 0.8 mol $L^{-1}$ . Then, NaDFP was added into the baseline electrolyte to prepare the NaDFP electrolyte, and NaDFP and

TMSB or TMSP were respectively added into the baseline electrolyte and assigned as NB or NP electrolyte. All electrolytes were prepared in a dry argon filled glove box with both moisture and oxygen concentrations below 0.1 ppm. NFM was purchased from Jiangsu Xiangying New Energy Technology Co, Ltd, HC was purchased from Kuraray Co Ltd. The pouch test cells with NFM cathode (120 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 0.1 C), HC anode (290 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 0.05 C), and Celgard 2700 separator were assembled using the conventional assembly method. Therein, NFM active material, polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF), carbon nanotube (CNT), conductive carbon black (Super P), and Maleic acid (the reason of addition maleic acid was shown in Table 1) were dispersed in N-methylpyrrolidone (NMP) with a mass ratio of 94.5:1.8:1:2.5:0.2, and the slurry was coated on an aluminum substrate to prepare the NFM cathode.

evidence_ledger.paper_id: 0156_Cai 等 - 2025 - A hard-soft synergy strategy enables drastic temperature performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries o
evidence_ledger.quote: With the help of "hard-soft synergy", polarization and capacity fading are alleviated signally during the cycling. Besides, rate performance of pouch cells is also improved by the synergistic effect of NP or NB electrolyte even at $-10^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ and $1\mathrm{C}$ , as shown in Fig. 4d and S5b. Furthermore, to evaluate dual additive potential at tougher low-temperatures, $-20^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ and $-30^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ discharge tests are necessary. Fig. 4e shows the capacity retention of pouch cells at different discharge currents, revealing the cells all can exhibit good electrochemical performance under the tested temperature conditions. Even at $-30^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ and $1\mathrm{C}$ , the discharge capacity of pouch cells with NP and NB electrolytes still achieves $729\mathrm{mAh}$ and $697\mathrm{mAh}$ , respectively. These results confirm that this co-additive addition strategy improves extremely low temperature performance of NFM/HC pouch cells. Summarily, compared to single additive or baseline electrolyte, NFM/HC pouch cells with multi-component functional electrolyte possess much better performance. Therein, the cells containing NP electrolyte have better room and high-temperature performance, and the cells containing NB electrolyte are more suitable for low-temperature application.

evidence_ledger.quote: In summary, a commercially feasible sodium-ion pouch cell with $Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ /hard carbon is fabricated in this work. According to the calculation of the frontier molecular orbital energy, the electrolyte additive adiponitrile (ADN) is selected as the electrolyte additive to improve the performance of sodium-ion battery for the first time, and the effects of the ADN on the performance improvement of the cathode material $Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ are investigated for the first time. The results show that ADN can promote the formation of highly conductive and stable SEI film on the cathode material surface, and effectively improve the high-low-temperature performance and cycling stability of $Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ as the cathode electrode material of sodium-ion batteries. In particular, the battery with 3% ADN shows the most obvious improvement, its discharge capacity increases by 10.5%, 8%, and 13% at the operating temperature of 45, -10, and -20 °C, respectively. For the cycling stability, the capacity retention rate of the battery without adding ADN drops rapidly to 75% after 40 cycles, while the capacity retention rate of the battery with 3% ADN can still reach 78% after 220 cycles. Adding ADN as electrolyte additive effectively improves the electrochemical performance of sodium ion batteries.

evidence_ledger.quote: $Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ , carbon nanotubes (CNTs), polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF), and carbon black with the mass ratio of 92.5: 2.0: 3.5: 2.0 were mixed in pyrrolidone to form a uniform slurry, and then coated on a 14 um thick aluminum foil to prepare the cathode electrode. The areal density was measured to be 10.0 mg cm $^{-2}$ , and the compacted density was 2.1 g cm $^{-3}$ . To prepare the anode electrode, hard carbon (Kuraray), carbon black, cellulose sodium (CMC), and styrene butadiene rubber (SBR) with the mass ratio of 94.5: 1.0: 2.0: 2.5 were added in deionized water and stirred into a uniform slurry, and then coated on a 9 um thick copper foil with the areal and compacted densities of 4.31 mg cm $^{-2}$ and 1.4 g cm $^{-3}$ , respectively. The cathode, anode, and separator (20 μm polypropylene) were assembled into pouch cells with a designed capacity of 650 mAh, and the thickness, width, and length were 10, 68, and 127 mm, respectively. The cells were dried in vacuum (-99 kPa/80 °C) until the water content was less than 150 ppm. At a dewpoint of -40 °C, the electrolytes defined as G1, G2, G3, and G4 (Table 1) were injected into the cells. After packaging in vacuum at room temperature for 48 hours; the pouch cells were placed at the environment with 0.8 MPa and 45 °C and charged at 0.05 C for 180 min, followed by another charge at a constant current of 0.1 C for 360 min.

evidence_ledger.quote: The sodium hexafluorophosphate (NaPF $_6$ , 99.8% min), diethylene glycol dimethyl ether (G2, 99.8% min) and 2-methyloxolane (MO, 99.8% min) were purchased from DoDo Chem. Common ether electrolyte (CCE) was prepared by dissolving 0.8 M NaPF $_6$ in G2 solvent. Weakly solvated electrolyte (WSE) was prepared by dissolving 0.8 M NaPF $_6$ in MO solvent. Co-intercalated electrolyte (CIE) was prepared by dissolving 0.8 M NaPF $_6$ in G2: MO = 7:3 vol%. All electrolyte preparation processes were carried out in a glovebox filled with Ar (H $_2$ O < 0.1 ppm and O $_2$ < 0.1 ppm). The electrolyte salts and solvents we purchased are of anhydrous grade. After purchase, they are placed in the glove box for direct use. Hard carbon (HC) materials were purchased from Baisige New Energy Co., Ltd. The HC negative electrode was prepared by mixing the active material, CMC (CMC2200, purchased from Daicel Corporation), SBR (BM-451B, purchased from Zeon Corporation) and conductive carbon black (weight ratio 92:1.5:3.5:3) in deionized water to form a homogeneous slurry. The slurry was spread on a copper foil (thickness 18 $\mu$ m) and dried at 80 °C for 8–12 h. Then, it was perforated into a circular electrode sheet with a diameter of 12 mm and a loading of 2.5–3.0 mg cm $^{-2}$ . Glass fiber (GF/D, Whatman) was used as separator and metallic sodium (purchased from Canrd Technology Co. Ltd.) was used as counter electrode.

evidence_ledger.quote: To verify the practical applicability of CIE, we assembled a 1.2 Ah (163 Wh kg $^{-1}$ ) pouch cell with O3-type NFM positive electrode and HC negative electrode (Fig. 6a). Figure 6b shows the cycling performance of the pouch cell at different temperatures. At 25 °C, the pouch cell provides a capacity of 1.18 Ah. As the temperature decreases, we verify the possibility of its operation at low temperatures, at -50 °C, the pouch cell still provides a capacity of 0.79 Ah (107 Wh kg $^{-1}$ ), demonstrating a significantly better low-temperature adaptability than that of conventional electrolytes. Moreover, even at -50 °C, the charge/discharge curve maintains a stable voltage plateau (Fig. 6c). Figure 6d shows the cycling performance of the pouch cell at -20 °C with 94.1% capacity retention after 300 cycles. In addition, in order to visually verify the practical application potential, the LED lights are continuously powered at a low temperature of -50 °C. The fully-charged state pouch cells keep the LED lights working for more than 10 hours (Fig. 6e). This demonstration confirms that the CIE has good prospects for practical applications, especially at low temperatures. We further compare our results with some previously reported low-temperature sodium-ion pouch cells (Fig. 6f, Table S6) $^{26,52-58}$ , and our work is comparable to most of the advanced reported works, which fully proves that the CIE developed by us has important application value for SIBs in cold environments.

evidence_ledger.quote: To evaluate the electrochemical performance of the electrolyte, Na $^{+}$ HC cells were assembled. The structural characteristics of HC are shown in Fig. S13, and for HC, the reversible capacity during the first cycle is critical for less sodium loss. As shown in Fig. 3a, CIE provides a specific capacity of 300.5 mAh g $^{-1}$ and an initial Coulombic efficiency (ICE) of 93.7% during the first cycle at 25°C, while CCE and WSE provide specific capacities of 299.6 and 300.1 mAh g $^{-1}$ and ICE of 87.7% and 91.4%, respectively. The three electrolytes deliver similar reversible capacities, while CIE has the highest ICE. The severe electrolyte decomposition creates a thick SEI and affects ICE $^{30,31}$ , which may explain the lower ICE of CCE. For CIE and WSE, the introduction of anions enables the construction of inorganic-rich SEI, and the appropriate number of anions in CIE consumes less Na $^{+}$ during film formation, thus guaranteeing a high ICE for HC in CIE. The rate performance of HC is shown in Figure S14, where CIE still provides a specific capacity of $195.0 \, mAh g^{-1}$ at $2 \, A g^{-1}$ , while CCE and WSE maintain a specific capacity of 204.6 and $131.4 \, mAh g^{-1}$ , respectively. This phenomenon suggests that the ionic conductivity plays a crucial role in the rate performance at $25^{\circ}C$ . The CIE effectively improves the ionic conductivity while retaining the co-intercalation behavior, so the rate performance is close to that of CCE.

evidence_ledger.quote: The Na||HC half cells with various electrolytes were assembled in Ar-filled gloveboxes using 2032-type coin cells with Na metal and HC. The amount of electrolyte was controlled at $100\mu \mathrm{L}$ for each Na||HC cell. The voltage ranges of Na||HC cells and HC||NFM pouch batteries were 0 to $2.5\mathrm{V}$ and 1.8 to $3.8\mathrm{V}$ , respectively. For pouch cells, cycle at $50\mathrm{mA}$ for $2\mathrm{h}$ , followed by $100\mathrm{mA}$ for $1\mathrm{h}$ , then $200\mathrm{mA}$ for $2.5\mathrm{h}$ . After a $36\mathrm{h}$ rest period, charge at $200\mathrm{mA}$ until full capacity is reached, then discharge to $1.8\mathrm{V}$ to complete the activation process. The entire procedure is conducted at 45 °C. The Na $^{+}$ storage performance was examined in a galvanostatic charge-discharge test on NEWARE Battery Test System (BTS-610, Shenzhen, China). The ion conductivity of the electrolyte was measured at different temperatures using the CHI660D electrochemical workstation through electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) technology. Galvanostatic intermittent titration technique (GITT) testing was performed by NEWARE battery system. The test was performed in the third charge-discharge cycle at 20 mA g $^{-1}$ with a pulse time for 30 min and the intervals for 2 h. Acquire 1 data point every 5 seconds. LSV (scan rate: 10 mV s $^{-1}$ , voltage range: 2.5–5.5 V) tests were implemented by CHI660D electrochemical workstation.

evidence_ledger.quote: In practical applications, the performance of SIBs under the low-temperature conditions has attracted more attention. Similarly, based on the actual use of SIBs, the impact of different electrolytes on the low-temperature performance of SIBs was also characterized by measuring the cycle performance and rate performance at $-10^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ , as well as the rate and discharge performance at $-20^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ and $-30^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ . Similar to high-temperature performance of pouch cells, these "hard-soft synergy" functional electrolytes induce amazing low-temperature performance of NFM/HC SIBs. As shown in the Figs 4a, 4b and S5a, both pouch cells with the NB or NP electrolyte can improve the cycling performance compared to the cells with the baseline electrolyte, an excellent capacity retention of $95\%$ after 350 cycles and high stability can be obtained benefiting from the "hard-soft synergy". Notably, though the capacity of the cells with NP or NB electrolyte both over $850\mathrm{mAh}$ (NB-859 mAh vs. NP-850 mAh) after 300 cycles, the NP group shows more fluctuant coulombic efficiency than the NB group, as shown in Fig. 4b. Additionally, the charge/discharge curves of the cells with NP, NB, and baseline electrolytes are shown in Fig. 4c. With the help of "hard-soft synergy", polarization and capacity fading are alleviated signally during the cycling.

evidence_ledger.quote: Taking into account the application environment temperature and corresponding performance requirements of the SIBs, the performance parameters of pouch cells under different temperature conditions after adding different electrolytes were evaluated in a targeted manner. In order to choose the optimal concentration, part of the tough condition performance corresponding to different addition amounts of two additives is shown in Fig. S3. Considering cost and performance comprehensively, a 1:1.5 proportioning of NaDFP to TMSB or TMSB is chosen as the most suitable ratio. First, under the room and high temperatures, the emphasis of pouch cells with different electrolytes was given to the rate, cycling and storage performance parameters. The pouch cells with NB, NP, or NaDFP-containing electrolytes generally exhibit higher performance parameters than the cells with the baseline electrolyte. Under the room temperature of 25 °C, as shown in the Fig. S4a and S4b, rate and cycling performance of the pouch cells with the NB and NP-containing electrolytes is improved comparing to the cells with the baseline electrolyte, which can easily ascribed to the superior conductivity and lower desolvation energy. To further verify the effect of NP, NB, and NaDFP electrolytes at tougher conditions, rate, cycling, and storage tests at 45 °C and 60 °C were performed.

evidence_ledger.quote: In summary, “hard-soft synergy” strategy—reasonably coupling NaDFP with TMSP or TMSB as the functional electrolytes successfully achieved wide-temperature performance of pouch SIBs over a range of $-30^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ to $60^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ . Benefit to the high-quality and rich element optimized NaDFP-based CEI/SEI layers on the electrode surfaces, and optimizing electrolyte structure which decrease the desolvation energy and induce superior electrolyte properties, a high capacity retention of $92\%$ after 350 cycles and a stable cycling performance at $1\mathrm{C}$ were achieved even at $-10^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ . Besides, both the discharge capacity at $-30^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ and the capacity retention after storage at $60^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ were also greatly improved. Importantly, only tiny dose of NaDFP, TMSB/TMSP with reasonably couple could enable considerably effective performance improvement of SIBs, which is essential to reduce the cost and advance the commercialization. This work not only obtains functional electrolytes for enhanced wide-temperature performance of NFM/HC SIBs, but also sheds lights on the designing multi-functional additive electrolytes of SIBs.

Abstract: A commercially feasible sodium-ion pouch cell with a capacity of 650 mAh is fabricated using the ternary layered $\mathrm{Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_2}$ and the hard carbon as the cathode and anode materials, respectively. $1.0\mathrm{MNaPF}_6$ in the mixed carbonate solvents is served as the electrolyte. According to the calculation of the frontier molecular orbital energy, adiponitrile (ADN) has a stronger ability of electron donating than the carbonate solvents and thus is easier to be reduced on the surface of the cathode material to form the solid-electrolyte interphase (SEI) film, so ADN is selected as the electrolyte additive to improve the performance of sodium-ion battery for the first time.
