2.2 Battery Assembly
$Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ , carbon nanotubes (CNTs), polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF), and carbon black with the mass ratio of 92.5: 2.0: 3.5: 2.0 were mixed in pyrrolidone to form a uniform slurry, and then coated on a 14 um thick aluminum foil to prepare the cathode electrode. The areal density was measured to be 10.0 mg cm $^{-2}$ , and the compacted density was 2.1 g cm $^{-3}$ . To prepare the anode electrode, hard carbon (Kuraray), carbon black, cellulose sodium (CMC), and styrene butadiene rubber (SBR) with the mass ratio of 94.5: 1.0: 2.0: 2.5 were added in deionized water and stirred into a uniform slurry, and then coated on a 9 um thick copper foil with the areal and compacted densities of 4.31 mg cm $^{-2}$ and 1.4 g cm $^{-3}$ , respectively. The cathode, anode, and separator (20 μm polypropylene) were assembled into pouch cells with a designed capacity of 650 mAh, and the thickness, width, and length were 10, 68, and 127 mm, respectively. The cells were dried in vacuum (-99 kPa/80 °C) until the water content was less than 150 ppm. At a dewpoint of -40 °C, the electrolytes defined as G1, G2, G3, and G4 (Table 1) were injected into the cells. After packaging in vacuum at room temperature for 48 hours; the pouch cells were placed at the environment with 0.8 MPa and 45 °C and charged at 0.05 C for 180 min, followed by another charge at a constant current of 0.1 C for 360 min. Then, the pouch cells were punctuated in vacuum to remove excess electrolyte and gas generated by the side reactions during the charge process. Eventually, the cells were packaged again and cut the air-bags to obtain the finished batteries for testing.

evidence_ledger.quote: The specific discharge capacities at different temperatures are shown in Fig. 4. At both high and low temperatures, the addition of ADN made the discharge capacity increase significantly, especially with the amount of 3%. This is because the additive ADN induces the formation of SEI film with low impedances. In particular, 3% ADN led to the formation of the SEI film with the lowest impedance and resulted in the lowest polarization. As a result, the batteries of G3 exhibited the highest discharge capacity retention rate at low temperatures. In addition, the batteries of G3 also exhibited the highest discharge capacity retention rate at high temperatures, indicating that the SEI film formed from the induction of ADN has a better stability at high temperatures. On the contrary, the discharge capacity retention rates of the batteries of G1 are the lowest at both high and low temperatures, demonstrating that the SEI film formed by the electrolyte without the additive ADN has large impedance and poor stability at high temperatures. To further understand the different rate and low-temperature performance of the batteries with different volume of electrolyte additive, the electrochemical impedance of each battery was tested (Fig. 5D). The electrochemical impedance spectra of the batteries of G1, G2, G3, and G4 showed flat semicircles in the high-frequency regions.

evidence_ledger.quote: To solve this problem, a CIE was designed in this work. The design principle is based on the following findings: there are always some solvents in the electrolyte that do not participate in the coordination and only act as ion transport media, which are called free solvents. For this reason, we replaced this part of free solvent with 2-methyloxolane (MO) which has a lower melting point ( $-136^{\circ}C$ , Table S1) and is less polar. Through this strategy, not only the co-embeddable solvation structure is retained and the ion transport kinetics are accelerated, but also the working temperature range of electrolyte in low-temperature environment is significantly widened by increasing the solvation entropy. To highlight the progressiveness of our designed electrolyte, we also used common co-intercalation ether electrolyte (CCE) and WSE as controls, and the specific electrolyte formulation is shown in Table S2. According to the optical photographs in Figure S1, CCE starts to have salt precipitation at $-30^{\circ}C$ , and it is even completely solidified at $-50^{\circ}C$ . On the other hand, WSE and our CIE remain liquid at $-50^{\circ}C$ , which effectively guarantees the possibility of electrolyte application at low temperatures. The ion transport mechanisms of various electrolytes at low temperatures are shown in Fig. 1, among which the CIE has the fastest ion transport rate due to the presence of the co-intercalation behavior.

The main raw materials used for preparing functional electrolytes, including EC, EMC, $NaPF_{6}$ , NaDFP, TMSP and TMSB were provided by the Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co, Ltd. The baseline electrolyte was prepared by dissolving $NaPF_{6}$ in a mixture of EC: EMC=3:7 to form a concentration of 0.8 mol $L^{-1}$ . Then, NaDFP was added into the baseline electrolyte to prepare the NaDFP electrolyte, and NaDFP and

TMSB or TMSP were respectively added into the baseline electrolyte and assigned as NB or NP electrolyte. All electrolytes were prepared in a dry argon filled glove box with both moisture and oxygen concentrations below 0.1 ppm. NFM was purchased from Jiangsu Xiangying New Energy Technology Co, Ltd, HC was purchased from Kuraray Co Ltd. The pouch test cells with NFM cathode (120 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 0.1 C), HC anode (290 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 0.05 C), and Celgard 2700 separator were assembled using the conventional assembly method. Therein, NFM active material, polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF), carbon nanotube (CNT), conductive carbon black (Super P), and Maleic acid (the reason of addition maleic acid was shown in Table 1) were dispersed in N-methylpyrrolidone (NMP) with a mass ratio of 94.5:1.8:1:2.5:0.2, and the slurry was coated on an aluminum substrate to prepare the NFM cathode.

citations.quote: In practical applications, the performance of SIBs under the low-temperature conditions has attracted more attention. Similarly, based on the actual use of SIBs, the impact of different electrolytes on the low-temperature performance of SIBs was also characterized by measuring the cycle performance and rate performance at $-10^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ , as well as the rate and discharge performance at $-20^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ and $-30^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ . Similar to high-temperature performance of pouch cells, these "hard-soft synergy" functional electrolytes induce amazing low-temperature performance of NFM/HC SIBs. As shown in the Figs 4a, 4b and S5a, both pouch cells with the NB or NP electrolyte can improve the cycling performance compared to the cells with the baseline electrolyte, an excellent capacity retention of $95\%$ after 350 cycles and high stability can be obtained benefiting from the "hard-soft synergy". Notably, though the capacity of the cells with NP or NB electrolyte both over $850\mathrm{mAh}$ (NB-859 mAh vs. NP-850 mAh) after 300 cycles, the NP group shows more fluctuant coulombic efficiency than the NB group, as shown in Fig. 4b. Additionally, the charge/discharge curves of the cells with NP, NB, and baseline electrolytes are shown in Fig. 4c. With the help of "hard-soft synergy", polarization and capacity fading are alleviated signally during the cycling.

citations.quote: Taking into account the application environment temperature and corresponding performance requirements of the SIBs, the performance parameters of pouch cells under different temperature conditions after adding different electrolytes were evaluated in a targeted manner. In order to choose the optimal concentration, part of the tough condition performance corresponding to different addition amounts of two additives is shown in Fig. S3. Considering cost and performance comprehensively, a 1:1.5 proportioning of NaDFP to TMSB or TMSB is chosen as the most suitable ratio. First, under the room and high temperatures, the emphasis of pouch cells with different electrolytes was given to the rate, cycling and storage performance parameters. The pouch cells with NB, NP, or NaDFP-containing electrolytes generally exhibit higher performance parameters than the cells with the baseline electrolyte. Under the room temperature of 25 °C, as shown in the Fig. S4a and S4b, rate and cycling performance of the pouch cells with the NB and NP-containing electrolytes is improved comparing to the cells with the baseline electrolyte, which can easily ascribed to the superior conductivity and lower desolvation energy. To further verify the effect of NP, NB, and NaDFP electrolytes at tougher conditions, rate, cycling, and storage tests at 45 °C and 60 °C were performed.

citations.quote: In summary, “hard-soft synergy” strategy—reasonably coupling NaDFP with TMSP or TMSB as the functional electrolytes successfully achieved wide-temperature performance of pouch SIBs over a range of $-30^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ to $60^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ . Benefit to the high-quality and rich element optimized NaDFP-based CEI/SEI layers on the electrode surfaces, and optimizing electrolyte structure which decrease the desolvation energy and induce superior electrolyte properties, a high capacity retention of $92\%$ after 350 cycles and a stable cycling performance at $1\mathrm{C}$ were achieved even at $-10^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ . Besides, both the discharge capacity at $-30^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ and the capacity retention after storage at $60^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ were also greatly improved. Importantly, only tiny dose of NaDFP, TMSB/TMSP with reasonably couple could enable considerably effective performance improvement of SIBs, which is essential to reduce the cost and advance the commercialization. This work not only obtains functional electrolytes for enhanced wide-temperature performance of NFM/HC SIBs, but also sheds lights on the designing multi-functional additive electrolytes of SIBs.

Abstract: A commercially feasible sodium-ion pouch cell with a capacity of 650 mAh is fabricated using the ternary layered $\mathrm{Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_2}$ and the hard carbon as the cathode and anode materials, respectively. $1.0\mathrm{MNaPF}_6$ in the mixed carbonate solvents is served as the electrolyte. According to the calculation of the frontier molecular orbital energy, adiponitrile (ADN) has a stronger ability of electron donating than the carbonate solvents and thus is easier to be reduced on the surface of the cathode material to form the solid-electrolyte interphase (SEI) film, so ADN is selected as the electrolyte additive to improve the performance of sodium-ion battery for the first time.

2.2 Battery Assembly
$Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ , carbon nanotubes (CNTs), polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF), and carbon black with the mass ratio of 92.5: 2.0: 3.5: 2.0 were mixed in pyrrolidone to form a uniform slurry, and then coated on a 14 um thick aluminum foil to prepare the cathode electrode. The areal density was measured to be 10.0 mg cm $^{-2}$ , and the compacted density was 2.1 g cm $^{-3}$ . To prepare the anode electrode, hard carbon (Kuraray), carbon black, cellulose sodium (CMC), and styrene butadiene rubber (SBR) with the mass ratio of 94.5: 1.0: 2.0: 2.5 were added in deionized water and stirred into a uniform slurry, and then coated on a 9 um thick copper foil with the areal and compacted densities of 4.31 mg cm $^{-2}$ and 1.4 g cm $^{-3}$ , respectively. The cathode, anode, and separator (20 μm polypropylene) were assembled into pouch cells with a designed capacity of 650 mAh, and the thickness, width, and length were 10, 68, and 127 mm, respectively. The cells were dried in vacuum (-99 kPa/80 °C) until the water content was less than 150 ppm. At a dewpoint of -40 °C, the electrolytes defined as G1, G2, G3, and G4 (Table 1) were injected into the cells. After packaging in vacuum at room temperature for 48 hours; the pouch cells were placed at the environment with 0.8 MPa and 45 °C and charged at 0.05 C for 180 min, followed by another charge at a constant current of 0.1 C for 360 min. Then, the pouch cells were punctuated in vacuum to remove excess electrolyte and gas generated by the side reactions during the charge process. Eventually, the cells were packaged again and cut the air-bags to obtain the finished batteries for testing.

citations.quote: In summary, a commercially feasible sodium-ion pouch cell with $Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ /hard carbon is fabricated in this work. According to the calculation of the frontier molecular orbital energy, the electrolyte additive adiponitrile (ADN) is selected as the electrolyte additive to improve the performance of sodium-ion battery for the first time, and the effects of the ADN on the performance improvement of the cathode material $Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ are investigated for the first time. The results show that ADN can promote the formation of highly conductive and stable SEI film on the cathode material surface, and effectively improve the high-low-temperature performance and cycling stability of $Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ as the cathode electrode material of sodium-ion batteries. In particular, the battery with 3% ADN shows the most obvious improvement, its discharge capacity increases by 10.5%, 8%, and 13% at the operating temperature of 45, -10, and -20 °C, respectively. For the cycling stability, the capacity retention rate of the battery without adding ADN drops rapidly to 75% after 40 cycles, while the capacity retention rate of the battery with 3% ADN can still reach 78% after 220 cycles. Adding ADN as electrolyte additive effectively improves the electrochemical performance of sodium ion batteries.

citations.quote: The specific discharge capacities at different temperatures are shown in Fig. 4. At both high and low temperatures, the addition of ADN made the discharge capacity increase significantly, especially with the amount of 3%. This is because the additive ADN induces the formation of SEI film with low impedances. In particular, 3% ADN led to the formation of the SEI film with the lowest impedance and resulted in the lowest polarization. As a result, the batteries of G3 exhibited the highest discharge capacity retention rate at low temperatures. In addition, the batteries of G3 also exhibited the highest discharge capacity retention rate at high temperatures, indicating that the SEI film formed from the induction of ADN has a better stability at high temperatures. On the contrary, the discharge capacity retention rates of the batteries of G1 are the lowest at both high and low temperatures, demonstrating that the SEI film formed by the electrolyte without the additive ADN has large impedance and poor stability at high temperatures. To further understand the different rate and low-temperature performance of the batteries with different volume of electrolyte additive, the electrochemical impedance of each battery was tested (Fig. 5D). The electrochemical impedance spectra of the batteries of G1, G2, G3, and G4 showed flat semicircles in the high-frequency regions.

citations.quote: The sodium hexafluorophosphate (NaPF $_6$ , 99.8% min), diethylene glycol dimethyl ether (G2, 99.8% min) and 2-methyloxolane (MO, 99.8% min) were purchased from DoDo Chem. Common ether electrolyte (CCE) was prepared by dissolving 0.8 M NaPF $_6$ in G2 solvent. Weakly solvated electrolyte (WSE) was prepared by dissolving 0.8 M NaPF $_6$ in MO solvent. Co-intercalated electrolyte (CIE) was prepared by dissolving 0.8 M NaPF $_6$ in G2: MO = 7:3 vol%. All electrolyte preparation processes were carried out in a glovebox filled with Ar (H $_2$ O < 0.1 ppm and O $_2$ < 0.1 ppm). The electrolyte salts and solvents we purchased are of anhydrous grade. After purchase, they are placed in the glove box for direct use. Hard carbon (HC) materials were purchased from Baisige New Energy Co., Ltd. The HC negative electrode was prepared by mixing the active material, CMC (CMC2200, purchased from Daicel Corporation), SBR (BM-451B, purchased from Zeon Corporation) and conductive carbon black (weight ratio 92:1.5:3.5:3) in deionized water to form a homogeneous slurry. The slurry was spread on a copper foil (thickness 18 $\mu$ m) and dried at 80 °C for 8–12 h. Then, it was perforated into a circular electrode sheet with a diameter of 12 mm and a loading of 2.5–3.0 mg cm $^{-2}$ . Glass fiber (GF/D, Whatman) was used as separator and metallic sodium (purchased from Canrd Technology Co. Ltd.) was used as counter electrode.

citations.quote: To solve this problem, a CIE was designed in this work. The design principle is based on the following findings: there are always some solvents in the electrolyte that do not participate in the coordination and only act as ion transport media, which are called free solvents. For this reason, we replaced this part of free solvent with 2-methyloxolane (MO) which has a lower melting point ( $-136^{\circ}C$ , Table S1) and is less polar. Through this strategy, not only the co-embeddable solvation structure is retained and the ion transport kinetics are accelerated, but also the working temperature range of electrolyte in low-temperature environment is significantly widened by increasing the solvation entropy. To highlight the progressiveness of our designed electrolyte, we also used common co-intercalation ether electrolyte (CCE) and WSE as controls, and the specific electrolyte formulation is shown in Table S2. According to the optical photographs in Figure S1, CCE starts to have salt precipitation at $-30^{\circ}C$ , and it is even completely solidified at $-50^{\circ}C$ . On the other hand, WSE and our CIE remain liquid at $-50^{\circ}C$ , which effectively guarantees the possibility of electrolyte application at low temperatures. The ion transport mechanisms of various electrolytes at low temperatures are shown in Fig. 1, among which the CIE has the fastest ion transport rate due to the presence of the co-intercalation behavior.

citations.quote: To verify the practical applicability of CIE, we assembled a 1.2 Ah (163 Wh kg $^{-1}$ ) pouch cell with O3-type NFM positive electrode and HC negative electrode (Fig. 6a). Figure 6b shows the cycling performance of the pouch cell at different temperatures. At 25 °C, the pouch cell provides a capacity of 1.18 Ah. As the temperature decreases, we verify the possibility of its operation at low temperatures, at -50 °C, the pouch cell still provides a capacity of 0.79 Ah (107 Wh kg $^{-1}$ ), demonstrating a significantly better low-temperature adaptability than that of conventional electrolytes. Moreover, even at -50 °C, the charge/discharge curve maintains a stable voltage plateau (Fig. 6c). Figure 6d shows the cycling performance of the pouch cell at -20 °C with 94.1% capacity retention after 300 cycles. In addition, in order to visually verify the practical application potential, the LED lights are continuously powered at a low temperature of -50 °C. The fully-charged state pouch cells keep the LED lights working for more than 10 hours (Fig. 6e). This demonstration confirms that the CIE has good prospects for practical applications, especially at low temperatures. We further compare our results with some previously reported low-temperature sodium-ion pouch cells (Fig. 6f, Table S6) $^{26,52-58}$ , and our work is comparable to most of the advanced reported works, which fully proves that the CIE developed by us has important application value for SIBs in cold environments.

citations.quote: To evaluate the electrochemical performance of the electrolyte, Na $^{+}$ HC cells were assembled. The structural characteristics of HC are shown in Fig. S13, and for HC, the reversible capacity during the first cycle is critical for less sodium loss. As shown in Fig. 3a, CIE provides a specific capacity of 300.5 mAh g $^{-1}$ and an initial Coulombic efficiency (ICE) of 93.7% during the first cycle at 25°C, while CCE and WSE provide specific capacities of 299.6 and 300.1 mAh g $^{-1}$ and ICE of 87.7% and 91.4%, respectively. The three electrolytes deliver similar reversible capacities, while CIE has the highest ICE. The severe electrolyte decomposition creates a thick SEI and affects ICE $^{30,31}$ , which may explain the lower ICE of CCE. For CIE and WSE, the introduction of anions enables the construction of inorganic-rich SEI, and the appropriate number of anions in CIE consumes less Na $^{+}$ during film formation, thus guaranteeing a high ICE for HC in CIE. The rate performance of HC is shown in Figure S14, where CIE still provides a specific capacity of $195.0 \, mAh g^{-1}$ at $2 \, A g^{-1}$ , while CCE and WSE maintain a specific capacity of 204.6 and $131.4 \, mAh g^{-1}$ , respectively. This phenomenon suggests that the ionic conductivity plays a crucial role in the rate performance at $25^{\circ}C$ . The CIE effectively improves the ionic conductivity while retaining the co-intercalation behavior, so the rate performance is close to that of CCE.

citations.quote: $\mathrm{LiPF_6}$ additive was incorporated in the pouch cell composed of the hard carbon/O3-type positive electrode and evaluated (Fig. 4a). The addition of the $\mathrm{LiPF_6}$ salt in the electrolyte improved capacity retention considerably compared with that of the typical FEC-added electrolyte. While the FEC-added pouch cell exhibited a capacity retention of $73.1\%$ at the 400th cycle, the addition of $\mathrm{LiPF_6}$ salt in the SIB electrolyte demonstrated a capacity retention of $92.7\%$ at the same cycle number. This achieved capacity retention is highly surpasses previously reported results, which is typically about $80\%$ (Table S1). The working nominal voltage change during the cycle indicates that the development of polarization from side reactions occurred in the case of the FEC-added cell (Fig. 4b). The working voltage with the $LiPF_{6}$ -added electrolyte was highly preserved in different cycles, implying that the energy delivered from the addition of the $LiPF_{6}$ pouch cell was well retained after the 400th cycle. Figure 4b demonstrates the cycle number-dependent voltage profiles obtained from hard carbon/O3-type positive electrode pouch cells. While polarization increased during repeated cycling in the FEC-added cell case, the $LiPF_{6}$ -added cell showed a stable voltage profile even after the 400th cycle.

The main raw materials used for preparing functional electrolytes, including EC, EMC, $NaPF_{6}$ , NaDFP, TMSP and TMSB were provided by the Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co, Ltd. The baseline electrolyte was prepared by dissolving $NaPF_{6}$ in a mixture of EC: EMC=3:7 to form a concentration of 0.8 mol $L^{-1}$ . Then, NaDFP was added into the baseline electrolyte to prepare the NaDFP electrolyte, and NaDFP and

TMSB or TMSP were respectively added into the baseline electrolyte and assigned as NB or NP electrolyte. All electrolytes were prepared in a dry argon filled glove box with both moisture and oxygen concentrations below 0.1 ppm. NFM was purchased from Jiangsu Xiangying New Energy Technology Co, Ltd, HC was purchased from Kuraray Co Ltd. The pouch test cells with NFM cathode (120 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 0.1 C), HC anode (290 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 0.05 C), and Celgard 2700 separator were assembled using the conventional assembly method. Therein, NFM active material, polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF), carbon nanotube (CNT), conductive carbon black (Super P), and Maleic acid (the reason of addition maleic acid was shown in Table 1) were dispersed in N-methylpyrrolidone (NMP) with a mass ratio of 94.5:1.8:1:2.5:0.2, and the slurry was coated on an aluminum substrate to prepare the NFM cathode.

citations.chunk_id: 0156_Cai 等 - 2025 - A hard-soft synergy strategy enables drastic temperature performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries o::sec8::child2
citations.quote: In practical applications, the performance of SIBs under the low-temperature conditions has attracted more attention. Similarly, based on the actual use of SIBs, the impact of different electrolytes on the low-temperature performance of SIBs was also characterized by measuring the cycle performance and rate performance at $-10^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ , as well as the rate and discharge performance at $-20^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ and $-30^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ . Similar to high-temperature performance of pouch cells, these "hard-soft synergy" functional electrolytes induce amazing low-temperature performance of NFM/HC SIBs. As shown in the Figs 4a, 4b and S5a, both pouch cells with the NB or NP electrolyte can improve the cycling performance compared to the cells with the baseline electrolyte, an excellent capacity retention of $95\%$ after 350 cycles and high stability can be obtained benefiting from the "hard-soft synergy". Notably, though the capacity of the cells with NP or NB electrolyte both over $850\mathrm{mAh}$ (NB-859 mAh vs. NP-850 mAh) after 300 cycles, the NP group shows more fluctuant coulombic efficiency than the NB group, as shown in Fig. 4b. Additionally, the charge/discharge curves of the cells with NP, NB, and baseline electrolytes are shown in Fig. 4c. With the help of "hard-soft synergy", polarization and capacity fading are alleviated signally during the cycling.

citations.quote: Taking into account the application environment temperature and corresponding performance requirements of the SIBs, the performance parameters of pouch cells under different temperature conditions after adding different electrolytes were evaluated in a targeted manner. In order to choose the optimal concentration, part of the tough condition performance corresponding to different addition amounts of two additives is shown in Fig. S3. Considering cost and performance comprehensively, a 1:1.5 proportioning of NaDFP to TMSB or TMSB is chosen as the most suitable ratio. First, under the room and high temperatures, the emphasis of pouch cells with different electrolytes was given to the rate, cycling and storage performance parameters. The pouch cells with NB, NP, or NaDFP-containing electrolytes generally exhibit higher performance parameters than the cells with the baseline electrolyte. Under the room temperature of 25 °C, as shown in the Fig. S4a and S4b, rate and cycling performance of the pouch cells with the NB and NP-containing electrolytes is improved comparing to the cells with the baseline electrolyte, which can easily ascribed to the superior conductivity and lower desolvation energy. To further verify the effect of NP, NB, and NaDFP electrolytes at tougher conditions, rate, cycling, and storage tests at 45 °C and 60 °C were performed.

citations.chunk_id: 0156_Cai 等 - 2025 - A hard-soft synergy strategy enables drastic temperature performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries o::sec10::child0
citations.quote: In summary, “hard-soft synergy” strategy—reasonably coupling NaDFP with TMSP or TMSB as the functional electrolytes successfully achieved wide-temperature performance of pouch SIBs over a range of $-30^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ to $60^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ . Benefit to the high-quality and rich element optimized NaDFP-based CEI/SEI layers on the electrode surfaces, and optimizing electrolyte structure which decrease the desolvation energy and induce superior electrolyte properties, a high capacity retention of $92\%$ after 350 cycles and a stable cycling performance at $1\mathrm{C}$ were achieved even at $-10^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ . Besides, both the discharge capacity at $-30^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ and the capacity retention after storage at $60^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ were also greatly improved. Importantly, only tiny dose of NaDFP, TMSB/TMSP with reasonably couple could enable considerably effective performance improvement of SIBs, which is essential to reduce the cost and advance the commercialization. This work not only obtains functional electrolytes for enhanced wide-temperature performance of NFM/HC SIBs, but also sheds lights on the designing multi-functional additive electrolytes of SIBs.

citations.quote: In practical applications, the performance of SIBs under the low-temperature conditions has attracted more attention. Similarly, based on the actual use of SIBs, the impact of different electrolytes on the low-temperature performance of SIBs was also characterized by measuring the cycle performance and rate performance at $-10^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ , as well as the rate and discharge performance at $-20^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ and $-30^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ . Similar to high-temperature performance of pouch cells, these "hard-soft synergy" functional electrolytes induce amazing low-temperature performance of NFM/HC SIBs. As shown in the Figs 4a, 4b and S5a, both pouch cells with the NB or NP electrolyte can improve the cycling performance compared to the cells with the baseline electrolyte, an excellent capacity retention of $95\%$ after 350 cycles and high stability can be obtained benefiting from the "hard-soft synergy". Notably, though the capacity of the cells with NP or NB electrolyte both over $850\mathrm{mAh}$ (NB-859 mAh vs. NP-850 mAh) after 300 cycles, the NP group shows more fluctuant coulombic efficiency than the NB group, as shown in Fig. 4b. Additionally, the charge/discharge curves of the cells with NP, NB, and baseline electrolytes are shown in Fig. 4c. With the help of "hard-soft synergy", polarization and capacity fading are alleviated signally during the cycling.

Xiaona Song $^{a,b}$ , Tao Meng $^{a}$ , Yaoming Deng $^{a,b}$ , Aimei Gao $^{a}$ , Junmin Nan $^{a}$ , Dong

Shu $^{a,c,d,*}$ , Fenyun Yi $^{a}$

Abstract: A commercially feasible sodium-ion pouch cell with a capacity of 650 mAh is fabricated using the ternary layered $\mathrm{Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_2}$ and the hard carbon as the cathode and anode materials, respectively. $1.0\mathrm{MNaPF}_6$ in the mixed carbonate solvents is served as the electrolyte. According to the calculation of the frontier molecular orbital energy, adiponitrile (ADN) has a stronger ability of electron donating than the carbonate solvents and thus is easier to be reduced on the surface of the cathode material to form the solid-electrolyte interphase (SEI) film, so ADN is selected as the electrolyte additive to improve the performance of sodium-ion battery for the first time.

citations.quote:
2.2 Battery Assembly
$Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ , carbon nanotubes (CNTs), polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF), and carbon black with the mass ratio of 92.5: 2.0: 3.5: 2.0 were mixed in pyrrolidone to form a uniform slurry, and then coated on a 14 um thick aluminum foil to prepare the cathode electrode. The areal density was measured to be 10.0 mg cm $^{-2}$ , and the compacted density was 2.1 g cm $^{-3}$ . To prepare the anode electrode, hard carbon (Kuraray), carbon black, cellulose sodium (CMC), and styrene butadiene rubber (SBR) with the mass ratio of 94.5: 1.0: 2.0: 2.5 were added in deionized water and stirred into a uniform slurry, and then coated on a 9 um thick copper foil with the areal and compacted densities of 4.31 mg cm $^{-2}$ and 1.4 g cm $^{-3}$ , respectively. The cathode, anode, and separator (20 μm polypropylene) were assembled into pouch cells with a designed capacity of 650 mAh, and the thickness, width, and length were 10, 68, and 127 mm, respectively. The cells were dried in vacuum (-99 kPa/80 °C) until the water content was less than 150 ppm. At a dewpoint of -40 °C, the electrolytes defined as G1, G2, G3, and G4 (Table 1) were injected into the cells. After packaging in vacuum at room temperature for 48 hours; the pouch cells were placed at the environment with 0.8 MPa and 45 °C and charged at 0.05 C for 180 min, followed by another charge at a constant current of 0.1 C for 360 min. Then, the pouch cells were punctuated in vacuum to remove excess electrolyte and gas generated by the side reactions during the charge process. Eventually, the cells were packaged again and cut the air-bags to obtain the finished batteries for testing.

citations.quote: In summary, a commercially feasible sodium-ion pouch cell with $Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ /hard carbon is fabricated in this work. According to the calculation of the frontier molecular orbital energy, the electrolyte additive adiponitrile (ADN) is selected as the electrolyte additive to improve the performance of sodium-ion battery for the first time, and the effects of the ADN on the performance improvement of the cathode material $Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ are investigated for the first time. The results show that ADN can promote the formation of highly conductive and stable SEI film on the cathode material surface, and effectively improve the high-low-temperature performance and cycling stability of $Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ as the cathode electrode material of sodium-ion batteries. In particular, the battery with 3% ADN shows the most obvious improvement, its discharge capacity increases by 10.5%, 8%, and 13% at the operating temperature of 45, -10, and -20 °C, respectively. For the cycling stability, the capacity retention rate of the battery without adding ADN drops rapidly to 75% after 40 cycles, while the capacity retention rate of the battery with 3% ADN can still reach 78% after 220 cycles. Adding ADN as electrolyte additive effectively improves the electrochemical performance of sodium ion batteries.

citations.chunk_id: 0061_Song 等 - 2018 - The effects of the functional electrolyte additive on the cathode material Na076Ni03Fe04Mn03O2 f::sec7::child4
citations.quote: The specific discharge capacities at different temperatures are shown in Fig. 4. At both high and low temperatures, the addition of ADN made the discharge capacity increase significantly, especially with the amount of 3%. This is because the additive ADN induces the formation of SEI film with low impedances. In particular, 3% ADN led to the formation of the SEI film with the lowest impedance and resulted in the lowest polarization. As a result, the batteries of G3 exhibited the highest discharge capacity retention rate at low temperatures. In addition, the batteries of G3 also exhibited the highest discharge capacity retention rate at high temperatures, indicating that the SEI film formed from the induction of ADN has a better stability at high temperatures. On the contrary, the discharge capacity retention rates of the batteries of G1 are the lowest at both high and low temperatures, demonstrating that the SEI film formed by the electrolyte without the additive ADN has large impedance and poor stability at high temperatures. To further understand the different rate and low-temperature performance of the batteries with different volume of electrolyte additive, the electrochemical impedance of each battery was tested (Fig. 5D). The electrochemical impedance spectra of the batteries of G1, G2, G3, and G4 showed flat semicircles in the high-frequency regions.

citations.chunk_id: 0033_Li 等 - 2026 - Enhanced sodium storage in hard carbon via solvent co-intercalation electrolyte enabling Ah-level po::sec7::child0
citations.quote: The sodium hexafluorophosphate (NaPF $_6$ , 99.8% min), diethylene glycol dimethyl ether (G2, 99.8% min) and 2-methyloxolane (MO, 99.8% min) were purchased from DoDo Chem. Common ether electrolyte (CCE) was prepared by dissolving 0.8 M NaPF $_6$ in G2 solvent. Weakly solvated electrolyte (WSE) was prepared by dissolving 0.8 M NaPF $_6$ in MO solvent. Co-intercalated electrolyte (CIE) was prepared by dissolving 0.8 M NaPF $_6$ in G2: MO = 7:3 vol%. All electrolyte preparation processes were carried out in a glovebox filled with Ar (H $_2$ O < 0.1 ppm and O $_2$ < 0.1 ppm). The electrolyte salts and solvents we purchased are of anhydrous grade. After purchase, they are placed in the glove box for direct use. Hard carbon (HC) materials were purchased from Baisige New Energy Co., Ltd. The HC negative electrode was prepared by mixing the active material, CMC (CMC2200, purchased from Daicel Corporation), SBR (BM-451B, purchased from Zeon Corporation) and conductive carbon black (weight ratio 92:1.5:3.5:3) in deionized water to form a homogeneous slurry. The slurry was spread on a copper foil (thickness 18 $\mu$ m) and dried at 80 °C for 8–12 h. Then, it was perforated into a circular electrode sheet with a diameter of 12 mm and a loading of 2.5–3.0 mg cm $^{-2}$ . Glass fiber (GF/D, Whatman) was used as separator and metallic sodium (purchased from Canrd Technology Co. Ltd.) was used as counter electrode.

citations.quote: To solve this problem, a CIE was designed in this work. The design principle is based on the following findings: there are always some solvents in the electrolyte that do not participate in the coordination and only act as ion transport media, which are called free solvents. For this reason, we replaced this part of free solvent with 2-methyloxolane (MO) which has a lower melting point ( $-136^{\circ}C$ , Table S1) and is less polar. Through this strategy, not only the co-embeddable solvation structure is retained and the ion transport kinetics are accelerated, but also the working temperature range of electrolyte in low-temperature environment is significantly widened by increasing the solvation entropy. To highlight the progressiveness of our designed electrolyte, we also used common co-intercalation ether electrolyte (CCE) and WSE as controls, and the specific electrolyte formulation is shown in Table S2. According to the optical photographs in Figure S1, CCE starts to have salt precipitation at $-30^{\circ}C$ , and it is even completely solidified at $-50^{\circ}C$ . On the other hand, WSE and our CIE remain liquid at $-50^{\circ}C$ , which effectively guarantees the possibility of electrolyte application at low temperatures. The ion transport mechanisms of various electrolytes at low temperatures are shown in Fig. 1, among which the CIE has the fastest ion transport rate due to the presence of the co-intercalation behavior.

citations.chunk_id: 0033_Li 等 - 2026 - Enhanced sodium storage in hard carbon via solvent co-intercalation electrolyte enabling Ah-level po::sec6::child0
citations.quote: To verify the practical applicability of CIE, we assembled a 1.2 Ah (163 Wh kg $^{-1}$ ) pouch cell with O3-type NFM positive electrode and HC negative electrode (Fig. 6a). Figure 6b shows the cycling performance of the pouch cell at different temperatures. At 25 °C, the pouch cell provides a capacity of 1.18 Ah. As the temperature decreases, we verify the possibility of its operation at low temperatures, at -50 °C, the pouch cell still provides a capacity of 0.79 Ah (107 Wh kg $^{-1}$ ), demonstrating a significantly better low-temperature adaptability than that of conventional electrolytes. Moreover, even at -50 °C, the charge/discharge curve maintains a stable voltage plateau (Fig. 6c). Figure 6d shows the cycling performance of the pouch cell at -20 °C with 94.1% capacity retention after 300 cycles. In addition, in order to visually verify the practical application potential, the LED lights are continuously powered at a low temperature of -50 °C. The fully-charged state pouch cells keep the LED lights working for more than 10 hours (Fig. 6e). This demonstration confirms that the CIE has good prospects for practical applications, especially at low temperatures. We further compare our results with some previously reported low-temperature sodium-ion pouch cells (Fig. 6f, Table S6) $^{26,52-58}$ , and our work is comparable to most of the advanced reported works, which fully proves that the CIE developed by us has important application value for SIBs in cold environments.

requirements.requirement: Cell is operated/cycled at -20 °C.
requirements.reasoning: Figure 6d reports cycling of the HC||NFM pouch cell at -20 °C with 94.1% capacity retention after 300 cycles, confirming operation at the target temperature.

requirements.reasoning: In Na||HC cells CIE delivers the highest first-cycle ICE (93.7%) versus CCE (87.7%) and WSE (91.4%) at 25 °C, and the mechanism (anion-rich, thinner SEI consuming less Na+) is explicitly attributed to the higher ICE; this ICE, however, is measured in the Na||HC half cell, not the full pouch cell.

citations.chunk_id: 0033_Li 等 - 2026 - Enhanced sodium storage in hard carbon via solvent co-intercalation electrolyte enabling Ah-level po::sec3::child0
citations.quote: To evaluate the electrochemical performance of the electrolyte, Na $^{+}$ HC cells were assembled. The structural characteristics of HC are shown in Fig. S13, and for HC, the reversible capacity during the first cycle is critical for less sodium loss. As shown in Fig. 3a, CIE provides a specific capacity of 300.5 mAh g $^{-1}$ and an initial Coulombic efficiency (ICE) of 93.7% during the first cycle at 25°C, while CCE and WSE provide specific capacities of 299.6 and 300.1 mAh g $^{-1}$ and ICE of 87.7% and 91.4%, respectively. The three electrolytes deliver similar reversible capacities, while CIE has the highest ICE. The severe electrolyte decomposition creates a thick SEI and affects ICE $^{30,31}$ , which may explain the lower ICE of CCE. For CIE and WSE, the introduction of anions enables the construction of inorganic-rich SEI, and the appropriate number of anions in CIE consumes less Na $^{+}$ during film formation, thus guaranteeing a high ICE for HC in CIE. The rate performance of HC is shown in Figure S14, where CIE still provides a specific capacity of $195.0 \, mAh g^{-1}$ at $2 \, A g^{-1}$ , while CCE and WSE maintain a specific capacity of 204.6 and $131.4 \, mAh g^{-1}$ , respectively. This phenomenon suggests that the ionic conductivity plays a crucial role in the rate performance at $25^{\circ}C$ . The CIE effectively improves the ionic conductivity while retaining the co-intercalation behavior, so the rate performance is close to that of CCE.

citations.quote: $\mathrm{LiPF_6}$ additive was incorporated in the pouch cell composed of the hard carbon/O3-type positive electrode and evaluated (Fig. 4a). The addition of the $\mathrm{LiPF_6}$ salt in the electrolyte improved capacity retention considerably compared with that of the typical FEC-added electrolyte. While the FEC-added pouch cell exhibited a capacity retention of $73.1\%$ at the 400th cycle, the addition of $\mathrm{LiPF_6}$ salt in the SIB electrolyte demonstrated a capacity retention of $92.7\%$ at the same cycle number. This achieved capacity retention is highly surpasses previously reported results, which is typically about $80\%$ (Table S1). The working nominal voltage change during the cycle indicates that the development of polarization from side reactions occurred in the case of the FEC-added cell (Fig. 4b). The working voltage with the $LiPF_{6}$ -added electrolyte was highly preserved in different cycles, implying that the energy delivered from the addition of the $LiPF_{6}$ pouch cell was well retained after the 400th cycle. Figure 4b demonstrates the cycle number-dependent voltage profiles obtained from hard carbon/O3-type positive electrode pouch cells. While polarization increased during repeated cycling in the FEC-added cell case, the $LiPF_{6}$ -added cell showed a stable voltage profile even after the 400th cycle.

citations.quote: While polarization increased during repeated cycling in the FEC-added cell case, the $LiPF_{6}$ -added cell showed a stable voltage profile even after the 400th cycle. The improved Coulombic efficiency was observed at pouch cell with $LiPF_{6}$ -added electrolyte than that of FEC-added electrolyte-injected cell (Fig. S8). Figure 4c, d shows the SEM images from the cycled hard carbon electrodes and O3-type positive electrodes that were dismantled from the cycled pouch cells. The hard carbon electrode cycled with the FEC-added electrolyte generated thick deposits on the surface from additional electrolyte decomposition during the various cycles. By contrast, the introduction of the $LiPF_{6}$ salt inhibited further deposition of SEI on the as-formed SEI because a less soluble and stable SEI was deposited after the formation process from the readily reducible, Li-solvated EC cluster. The C 1s XPS spectra also implied that the additional SEI deposition was suppressed following the addition of $LiPF_{6}$ after cycling (Fig. S9). Energy-dispersive spectroscopic analysis at the corresponding SEM image revealed an increased concentration of oxygen species at the hard carbon electrode cycled with FEC-added electrolyte, while the cycled hard carbon with $LiPF_{6}$ -added electrolyte demonstrated a restrained increment in the oxygen species, which could be attributed to the reduction in carbonate electrolytes (Fig. S10).

citations.quote: The coin half-cell evaluation was performed with stacked electrode with sodium metal chip/glass filter/O3-type positive electrode and hard carbon electrode, respectively. After injecting the electrolyte and the additive-added electrolyte in 2032 coin cell, the sodium half-cell was aged for 24 h at room temperature to soak electrolyte. After aging, three cycles of the 0.1 C CC-CV (with 0.05 C cutoff) charge and followed 0.1 C CC discharge was performed for formation process with voltage range of 2.0–4.0 V (vs. Na/Na $^{+}$ ) and 0.0–1.5 V (vs. Na/Na $^{+}$ ) for O3-type positive electrode and hard carbon electrode, respectively, at room temperature. The 0.5 C CC-CV (with 0.05 C cutoff) charge and 0.5 C CC discharge was performed for room temperature cycling with voltage range of 2.0–4.0 V (vs. Na/Na $^{+}$ ) and 0.0–1.5 V (vs. Na/Na $^{+}$ ) for O3-type positive electrode and hard carbon electrode, respectively. After injecting the electrolyte and the additive-added electrolyte, the cell was pressed to 1.0 MPa using a jig to evaluate its electrochemical cycling performance. Before electrochemical characterization, the pouch cell was rested for 24 h at room temperature. The pouch cell formation was performed with a CC-CV charge of 0.1 C (with a 0.05 C cutoff) and with a CC discharge of 0.1 C, over a voltage range of 2.5–4.0 V.

## 配方筛选结果 已整理候选资料，当前暂缓推荐。未满足的条件列在下方。 ### 候选资料：c1-NB-NaDFP-TMSB（尚未获推荐） 以下为候选记录中的组成，配制时须核对所引原文的比例基准与用量。 盐：NaPF6；浓度：0.8 mol L⁻¹；NaPF6：0.8 mol L⁻¹；溶剂：EC, EMC；溶剂比例（基准待核对）：EC=0.3, EMC=0.7；添加剂：NaDFP, TMSB；添加剂用量：NaDFP:TMSB=1:1.5 (原文给出比例；绝对值 wt% 未在检索到的原文中出现)。 - 配方原文 [0156_Cai 等 - 2025 - A hard-soft synergy strategy enables drastic temperature performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries o::sec4::child0]：The main raw materials used for preparing functional electrolytes, including EC, EMC, $NaPF_{6}$ , NaDFP, TMSP and TMSB were provided by the Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co, Ltd. The baseline electrolyte was prepared by dissolving $NaPF_{6}$ in a mixture of EC: EMC=3:7 to form a concentration of 0.8 mol $L^{-1}$ . Then, NaDFP was added into the baseline electrolyte to prepare the NaDFP electrolyte, and NaDFP and TMSB or TMSP were respectively added into the baseline electrolyte and assigned as NB or NP electrolyte. All electrolytes were prepared in a dry argon filled glove box with both moisture and oxygen concentrations below 0.1 ppm. NFM was purchased from Jiangsu Xiangying New Energy Technology Co, Ltd, HC was purchased from Kuraray Co Ltd. The pouch test cells with NFM cathode (120 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 0.1 C), HC anode (290 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 0.05 C), and Celgard 2700 separator were assembled using the conventional assembly method. Therein, NFM active material, polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF), carbon nanotube (CNT), conductive carbon black (Super P), and Maleic acid (the reason of addition maleic acid was shown in Table 1) were dispersed in N-methylpyrrolidone (NMP) with a mass ratio of 94.5:1.8:1:2.5:0.2, and the slurry was coated on an aluminum substrate to prepare the NFM cathode. ### 候选资料：c2-NP-NaDFP-TMSP（尚未获推荐） 以下为候选记录中的组成，配制时须核对所引原文的比例基准与用量。 盐：NaPF6；浓度：0.8 mol L⁻¹；NaPF6：0.8 mol L⁻¹；溶剂：EC, EMC；溶剂比例（基准待核对）：EC=0.3, EMC=0.7；添加剂：NaDFP, TMSP；添加剂用量：NaDFP:TMSP=1:1.5 (原文给出比例；绝对值 wt% 未在检索到的原文中出现)。 - 配方原文 [0156_Cai 等 - 2025 - A hard-soft synergy strategy enables drastic temperature performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries o::sec4::child0]：The main raw materials used for preparing functional electrolytes, including EC, EMC, $NaPF_{6}$ , NaDFP, TMSP and TMSB were provided by the Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co, Ltd. The baseline electrolyte was prepared by dissolving $NaPF_{6}$ in a mixture of EC: EMC=3:7 to form a concentration of 0.8 mol $L^{-1}$ . Then, NaDFP was added into the baseline electrolyte to prepare the NaDFP electrolyte, and NaDFP and TMSB or TMSP were respectively added into the baseline electrolyte and assigned as NB or NP electrolyte. All electrolytes were prepared in a dry argon filled glove box with both moisture and oxygen concentrations below 0.1 ppm. NFM was purchased from Jiangsu Xiangying New Energy Technology Co, Ltd, HC was purchased from Kuraray Co Ltd. The pouch test cells with NFM cathode (120 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 0.1 C), HC anode (290 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 0.05 C), and Celgard 2700 separator were assembled using the conventional assembly method. Therein, NFM active material, polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF), carbon nanotube (CNT), conductive carbon black (Super P), and Maleic acid (the reason of addition maleic acid was shown in Table 1) were dispersed in N-methylpyrrolidone (NMP) with a mass ratio of 94.5:1.8:1:2.5:0.2, and the slurry was coated on an aluminum substrate to prepare the NFM cathode. ### 候选资料：c3-G3-ADN3（尚未获推荐） 以下为候选记录中的组成，配制时须核对所引原文的比例基准与用量。 盐：NaPF6；浓度：1 mol L⁻¹；NaPF6：1 mol L⁻¹；溶剂：EC, PC, DEC；溶剂比例（基准待核对）：EC=0.25, PC=0.25, DEC=0.5；添加剂：FEC, ADN；添加剂用量：FEC=5%, ADN=3%。 - 配方原文 [0061_Song 等 - 2018 - The effects of the functional electrolyte additive on the cathode material Na076Ni03Fe04Mn03O2 f::sec11::child0]：Table 1 The contents of each component in four groups of electrolytes Table 2 Calculated frontier molecular orbital energy levels of several carbonate molecules (EC, DEC, PC) and ADN Table 1 The contents of each component in four groups of electrolytes

### 候选资料：c4-CIE-G2-MO（尚未获推荐） 以下为候选记录中的组成，配制时须核对所引原文的比例基准与用量。 盐：NaPF6；浓度：0.8 mol L⁻¹；NaPF6：0.8 mol L⁻¹；溶剂：G2 (DEGDME), MO (2-methyloxolane)；溶剂比例（体积）：G2 (DEGDME)=0.7, MO (2-methyloxolane)=0.3。 - 配方原文 [0033_Li 等 - 2026 - Enhanced sodium storage in hard carbon via solvent co-intercalation electrolyte enabling Ah-level po::sec7::child0]：The sodium hexafluorophosphate (NaPF $_6$ , 99.8% min), diethylene glycol dimethyl ether (G2, 99.8% min) and 2-methyloxolane (MO, 99.8% min) were purchased from DoDo Chem. Common ether electrolyte (CCE) was prepared by dissolving 0.8 M NaPF $_6$ in G2 solvent. Weakly solvated electrolyte (WSE) was prepared by dissolving 0.8 M NaPF $_6$ in MO solvent. Co-intercalated electrolyte (CIE) was prepared by dissolving 0.8 M NaPF $_6$ in G2: MO = 7:3 vol%. All electrolyte preparation processes were carried out in a glovebox filled with Ar (H $_2$ O < 0.1 ppm and O $_2$ < 0.1 ppm). The electrolyte salts and solvents we purchased are of anhydrous grade. After purchase, they are placed in the glove box for direct use. Hard carbon (HC) materials were purchased from Baisige New Energy Co., Ltd. The HC negative electrode was prepared by mixing the active material, CMC (CMC2200, purchased from Daicel Corporation), SBR (BM-451B, purchased from Zeon Corporation) and conductive carbon black (weight ratio 92:1.5:3.5:3) in deionized water to form a homogeneous slurry. The slurry was spread on a copper foil (thickness 18 $\mu$ m) and dried at 80 °C for 8–12 h. Then, it was perforated into a circular electrode sheet with a diameter of 12 mm and a loading of 2.5–3.0 mg cm $^{-2}$ . Glass fiber (GF/D, Whatman) was used as separator and metallic sodium (purchased from Canrd Technology Co. Ltd.) was used as counter electrode. ### 候选资料：c5-LiPF6-additive（尚未获推荐） 以下为候选记录中的组成，配制时须核对所引原文的比例基准与用量。 盐：NaPF6；总盐浓度：1.2 mol L⁻¹；NaPF6：1 mol L⁻¹；LiPF6：0.2 mol L⁻¹；溶剂：EC, DMC；溶剂比例（体积）：EC=0.5, DMC=0.5；添加剂：FEC, LiPF6；添加剂用量：FEC=0.5 wt%, LiPF6=0.2 M。 - 配方原文 [0125_0141_Transformative_Effect_of_Li_Salt_for_Pro::sec4::child0]：0.5 wt% FEC (Soulbrain), 0.2 M LiPF $_{6}$ (Chunbo), and 0.2 M lithium difluoro(oxalato)borate (LiODFB) were added to 1.0 M NaPF $_{6}$ EC/DMC (1:1 = v/v, Dongwha Electrolyte), respectively. This mixture was prepared in an Ar-filled glove box and stirred overnight. The ionic conductivities of electrolytes were measured at 22 °C with a conductivity meter (Oakton CON 6+). ## 候选评估 ### c1-NB-NaDFP-TMSB 评估建议：Composition identity, full-cell system and low-temperature suitability are directly supported, but the specific target of improving initial Coulombic efficiency after formation is not evidenced (first-cycle CE is only reported as differing, without direction or value), so a recommend decision cannot be substantiated; hold pending ICE-resolving evidence. 任务要求与已有依据（模型语义判断，程序核验出处）： - Electrolyte intended for a hard-carbon anode || layered-oxide (NFM) cathode sodium-ion pouch full cell.：The paper assembles NFM/HC pouch test cells and evaluates the NB (NaDFP+TMSB) electrolyte in them, matching the candidate's target full-cell system. [0156_Cai 等 - 2025 - A hard-soft synergy strategy enables drastic temperature performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries o::sec4::child0][0156_Cai 等 - 2025 - A hard-soft synergy strategy enables drastic temperature performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries o::sec8::child2] - Salt/solvent/concentration identity: NaPF6 at 0.8 mol/L in EC:EMC = 3:7.：The baseline electrolyte is explicitly prepared by dissolving NaPF6 in EC:EMC=3:7 at 0.8 mol/L, exactly the candidate's salt system and concentration. [0156_Cai 等 - 2025 - A hard-soft synergy strategy enables drastic temperature performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries o::sec4::child0] - Additive combination NaDFP + TMSB at a 1:1.5 ratio (the NB electrolyte).：NaDFP with TMSB is defined as the NB electrolyte, and a 1:1.5 NaDFP:TMSB proportion is chosen as the most suitable ratio, matching the candidate's additive pair and ratio. [0156_Cai 等 - 2025 - A hard-soft synergy strategy enables drastic temperature performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries o::sec4::child0][0156_Cai 等 - 2025 - A hard-soft synergy strategy enables drastic temperature performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries o::sec8::child0] - Suitability for low-temperature operation around -20 degrees C in the pouch full cell.：The paper characterizes -20 degrees C rate/discharge performance and explicitly states the NB (NaDFP+TMSB) cells are more suitable for low-temperature application. [0156_Cai 等 - 2025 - A hard-soft synergy strategy enables drastic temperature performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries o::sec8::child2][0156_Cai 等 - 2025 - A hard-soft synergy strategy enables drastic temperature performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries o::sec8::child3] - Improves the initial Coulombic efficiency after formation for this candidate.：The only relevant chunk reports that first-cycle coulombic efficiencies of pouch NFM/HC cells differ with additives and that film formation changed, but it gives no value or direction showing NB achieves a higher initial CE than baseline; the ICE-improvement claim is therefore not established for this candidate. [0156_Cai 等 - 2025 - A hard-soft synergy strategy enables drastic temperature performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries o::sec7::child8] 文献与候选的关联：The candidate maps to the paper's NB electrolyte: same NaPF6/EC:EMC=3:7 base, same NaDFP+TMSB pair at 1:1.5, tested in NFM/HC pouch cells; the low-temperature association holds, but no experiment associates this candidate with an improved initial Coulombic efficiency value or direction. [0156_Cai 等 - 2025 - A hard-soft synergy strategy enables drastic temperature performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries o::sec4::child0][0156_Cai 等 - 2025 - A hard-soft synergy strategy enables drastic temperature performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries o::sec8::child0] ### c2-NP-NaDFP-TMSP 评估建议：候选配方身份与原文 NP 电解液完全对应，且体系为目标型硬碳||层状氧化物软包全电池、低温可运行，属于有文献支持的可用配方；但本任务核心目标——化成后 ICE 的提升——缺少该候选的定量证据，且原文相对性结论显示低温应用更倾向 NB（NaDFP+TMSB），故在获得 ICE 直接数据前不宜给出推荐，判定为 hold。本评估仅依据文献与已记录的预测（本轮无 computation refs），不表示已做新实验。 任务要求与已有依据（模型语义判断，程序核验出处）： - 目标电芯为硬碳负极||层状氧化物正极的钠离子软包全电池：原文的正极 NFM 即层状氧化物 NaNi0.33Fe0.33Mn0.33O2，负极 HC（硬碳），并以 pouch cells 形式组装测评，与目标电芯构型一致。 [0156_Cai 等 - 2025 - A hard-soft synergy strategy enables drastic temperature performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries o::sec4::child0][0156_Cai 等 - 2025 - A hard-soft synergy strategy enables drastic temperature performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries o::sec8::child3] - 基础电解液为 NaPF6 0.8 mol/L 溶于 EC:EMC = 3:7：原文明确 baseline electrolyte 为 NaPF6 溶于 EC:EMC=3:7、浓度 0.8 mol/L，与候选的盐、浓度、溶剂比例一致。 [0156_Cai 等 - 2025 - A hard-soft synergy strategy enables drastic temperature performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries o::sec4::child0] - 候选采用 NaDFP + TMSP 双添加剂（NP 电解液）：原文将 NaDFP 与 TMSP（或 TMSB）分别加入 baseline 并命名为 NP（NaDFP+TMSP），候选成分为 NaDFP+TMSP，与 NP 电解液身份对应。 [0156_Cai 等 - 2025 - A hard-soft synergy strategy enables drastic temperature performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries o::sec4::child0][0156_Cai 等 - 2025 - A hard-soft synergy strategy enables drastic temperature performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries o::sec10::child0] - NaDFP:TMSP 添加比例为 1:1.5：原文称综合考虑成本与性能选取 NaDFP 与 TMSB/TMSP 的 1:1.5 比例（原文该句存在 TMSB/TMSP 笔误），支持该比例作为 TMSP 体系的最优比。 [0156_Cai 等 - 2025 - A hard-soft synergy strategy enables drastic temperature performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries o::sec8::child0] - 候选适用于 -20 ℃ 低温工况的软包全电池：原文以 -20 ℃ 和 -30 ℃ 的倍率/放电测试表征低低温性能，NP 与 NB 电解液电池均表现出良好电化学性能（-30 ℃ 1C 下 NP 达 729 mAh），说明该候选在低温可运行；但原文相对性结论认为 NB 更适低温，NP 更适常温/高温。 [0156_Cai 等 - 2025 - A hard-soft synergy strategy enables drastic temperature performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries o::sec8::child2][0156_Cai 等 - 2025 - A hard-soft synergy strategy enables drastic temperature performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries o::sec8::child3] - 候选能提高化成后的首次库仑效率（ICE）：原文仅以 Fig. 3h 指出不同添加剂下 NFM/HC 软包首圈库仑效率不同、成膜过程改变，并只给出 NP/NB 相对 baseline 与 NaDFP 的定性预期，未提供 NP 候选 ICE 的具体数值或与 baseline 的直接对比，故无法据文献确认其对 ICE 的提升。 [0156_Cai 等 - 2025 - A hard-soft synergy strategy enables drastic temperature performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries o::sec7::child8] - 评测基于化成（formation）之后的电池状态：原文描述了软包电池老化与化成步骤（室温充至 2.0 V，再 45 ℃、90 mA 充至 3.8 V），说明后续性能测评是在化成之后进行，符合问题对化成后 ICE 的语境。 [0156_Cai 等 - 2025 - A hard-soft synergy strategy enables drastic temperature performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries o::sec5::child0] 文献与候选的关联：候选 c2 的盐、浓度、溶剂比、添加剂与比例均与原文 NP 电解液（NaPF6 0.8 M, EC:EMC=3:7, NaDFP+TMSP 1:1.5）逐一对应，且原文测评体系为目标型的 NFM/HC 软包全电池，故候选身份与文献实验体系可建立关联；但原文未就 ICE 给出该候选的定量结果，且低温相对性结论偏向 NB，因此关联只支持‘该配方为文献报道的软包电解液’，不构成其对 -20 ℃ 化成后 ICE 提升的直接验证。 [0156_Cai 等 - 2025 - A hard-soft synergy strategy enables drastic temperature performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries o::sec4::child0][0156_Cai 等 - 2025 - A hard-soft synergy strategy enables drastic temperature performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries o::sec8::child0] ### c3-G3-ADN3 评估建议：The candidate matches a documented formulation (G3) that improves -20 °C performance in the target hard-carbon || layered-oxide pouch full cell, but no ICE-after-formation data is reported, so the specific selection objective is not yet evidenced and the decision is held pending that measurement. 任务要求与已有依据（模型语义判断，程序核验出处）： - Candidate electrolyte identity matches the tested formulation: 1.0 M NaPF6 in EC/PC/DEC (25/25/50) with 5% FEC and 3% ADN (G3).：Table 1 lists G3 as EC 25%, PC 25%, DEC 50%, FEC 5%, ADN 3%, NaPF6 1.0 M, which exactly matches the candidate composition. [0061_Song 等 - 2018 - The effects of the functional electrolyte additive on the cathode material Na076Ni03Fe04Mn03O2 f::sec11][0061_Song 等 - 2018 - The effects of the functional electrolyte additive on the cathode material Na076Ni03Fe04Mn03O2 f::sec11::child0] - Target system is a hard-carbon || layered-oxide sodium-ion pouch full cell.：The abstract and assembly section describe a pouch cell using Na0.76Ni0.3Fe0.4Mn0.3O2 cathode and hard carbon anode with designed capacity 650 mAh, i.e. the target full-cell configuration. [0061_Song 等 - 2018 - The effects of the functional electrolyte additive on the cathode material Na076Ni03Fe04Mn03O2 f::sec2::child0][0061_Song 等 - 2018 - The effects of the functional electrolyte additive on the cathode material Na076Ni03Fe04Mn03O2 f::sec5] - -20 °C low-temperature performance improvement by the 3% ADN electrolyte.：The paper reports that the battery with 3% ADN shows a 13% discharge capacity increase at -20 °C, and that G3 exhibits the highest low-temperature discharge capacity retention, attributed to a low-impedance SEI. [0061_Song 等 - 2018 - The effects of the functional electrolyte additive on the cathode material Na076Ni03Fe04Mn03O2 f::sec8::child0][0061_Song 等 - 2018 - The effects of the functional electrolyte additive on the cathode material Na076Ni03Fe04Mn03O2 f::sec7::child4] - Improvement of initial Coulombic efficiency (ICE) after formation.：The sources report OCV, formation charge protocol, charge/discharge capacities, rate, low-temperature and cycling performance, but never report or compute an initial Coulombic efficiency for G3 relative to G1; the SEI-formation discussion does not quantify ICE. 文献与候选的关联：The candidate composition corresponds to electrolyte G3 in Table 1, one of the electrolytes injected into the Na0.76Ni0.3Fe0.4Mn0.3O2 || hard-carbon pouch cells described in the assembly section, so the electrochemical results can be associated with this candidate. [0061_Song 等 - 2018 - The effects of the functional electrolyte additive on the cathode material Na076Ni03Fe04Mn03O2 f::sec11][0061_Song 等 - 2018 - The effects of the functional electrolyte additive on the cathode material Na076Ni03Fe04Mn03O2 f::sec5::child0] ### c4-CIE-G2-MO 评估建议：The candidate is exactly the paper's CIE (0.8 M NaPF6 in G2:MO 7:3 vol%), which shows the highest HC first-cycle ICE among the compared electrolytes and enables an Ah-level HC||NFM pouch cell that operates at -20 °C, so the literature supports this intervention for improving ICE in the target low-temperature full cell; the only gap is that the ICE at -20 °C is not separately reported for the pouch cell. 任务要求与已有依据（模型语义判断，程序核验出处）： - Electrolyte formulation matches: 0.8 M NaPF6 dissolved in G2:MO = 7:3 by volume, no additives.：The Materials section reports the co-intercalated electrolyte (CIE) as 0.8 M NaPF6 in G2:MO = 7:3 vol%, exactly matching the candidate salt, concentration, solvents and ratio; no additive is listed. [0033_Li 等 - 2026 - Enhanced sodium storage in hard carbon via solvent co-intercalation electrolyte enabling Ah-level po::sec7::child0] - Candidate is the co-intercalation ether electrolyte (CIE) intended to bypass desolvation and improve HC first-cycle reversibility.：The paper states the CIE was designed by replacing free solvent with low-melting MO in G2 to retain co-embedding, widen the low-temperature range and form a thin inorganic-rich SEI, which is the mechanism behind improved ICE. [0033_Li 等 - 2026 - Enhanced sodium storage in hard carbon via solvent co-intercalation electrolyte enabling Ah-level po::sec2::child1] - Target system is a hard-carbon negative electrode paired with a layered-oxide positive electrode in an Ah-level pouch full cell.：A 1.2 Ah pouch cell was assembled with O3-type NaNi1/3Fe1/3Mn1/3O2 (layered oxide) positive electrode and HC negative electrode, matching the required HC||layered-oxide pouch configuration. [0033_Li 等 - 2026 - Enhanced sodium storage in hard carbon via solvent co-intercalation electrolyte enabling Ah-level po::sec6::child0] - Cell is operated/cycled at -20 °C.：Figure 6d reports cycling of the HC||NFM pouch cell at -20 °C with 94.1% capacity retention after 300 cycles, confirming operation at the target temperature. [0033_Li 等 - 2026 - Enhanced sodium storage in hard carbon via solvent co-intercalation electrolyte enabling Ah-level po::sec6::child0] - The intervention improves initial Coulombic efficiency of the hard-carbon electrode.：In Na||HC cells CIE delivers the highest first-cycle ICE (93.7%) versus CCE (87.7%) and WSE (91.4%) at 25 °C, and the mechanism (anion-rich, thinner SEI consuming less Na+) is explicitly attributed to the higher ICE; this ICE, however, is measured in the Na||HC half cell, not the full pouch cell. [0033_Li 等 - 2026 - Enhanced sodium storage in hard carbon via solvent co-intercalation electrolyte enabling Ah-level po::sec3::child0] - ICE after formation is reported at -20 °C in the HC||layered-oxide pouch full cell itself.：ICE values are given only for Na||HC half cells (93.7% at 25 °C, 80.5% at -50 °C); the pouch full cell results at -20 °C report capacity retention, not ICE, and no explicit transfer of the half-cell ICE to the -20 °C full cell is stated, so the target-specific metric is unverified. [0033_Li 等 - 2026 - Enhanced sodium storage in hard carbon via solvent co-intercalation electrolyte enabling Ah-level po::sec6::child0] 文献与候选的关联：The ICE evidence (93.7% for CIE, highest among the three electrolytes) is obtained in Na||HC coin half cells at 25 °C, whereas the pouch cell with matching NFM/HC configuration reports capacity/energy and -20 °C cycling retention rather than ICE; the candidate composition is identical to the reported CIE, but the ICE measurement and the full-cell performance come from different cell formats. [0033_Li 等 - 2026 - Enhanced sodium storage in hard carbon via solvent co-intercalation electrolyte enabling Ah-level po::sec3::child0][0033_Li 等 - 2026 - Enhanced sodium storage in hard carbon via solvent co-intercalation electrolyte enabling Ah-level po::sec6::child0] ### c5-LiPF6-additive 评估建议：The assessment is complete: LiPF6 is supported as an intervention for the hard carbon/O3 layered-oxide pouch cell, but the candidate's combined FEC+LiPF6 composition is not the tested formulation and there is no evidence addressing initial Coulombic efficiency after formation or -20 °C operation, so the candidate cannot yet be recommended. 任务要求与已有依据（模型语义判断，程序核验出处）： - Electrolyte intervention applied in a hard-carbon||layered-oxide sodium-ion pouch full cell：The source describes a pouch cell composed of hard carbon and an O3-type layered oxide positive electrode, which is the target full-cell configuration. [0125_0141_Transformative_Effect_of_Li_Salt_for_Pro::sec13::child0] - LiPF6 additive as the intervention for the hard carbon / layered-oxide cell：LiPF6 was marginally added to the 1.0 M NaPF6 EC/DMC electrolyte and the LiPF6-added pouch cell retained 92.7% capacity versus 73.1% for the FEC-added cell, establishing LiPF6 as the studied intervention. [0125_0141_Transformative_Effect_of_Li_Salt_for_Pro::sec13::child0][0125_0141_Transformative_Effect_of_Li_Salt_for_Pro::sec14::child1] - Improvement of initial Coulombic efficiency after formation：The source reports improved Coulombic efficiency for the LiPF6-added pouch cell versus the FEC-added cell and suppressed post-formation SEI deposition, but it does not report initial Coulombic efficiency values measured after formation, so this specific metric is not established. [0125_0141_Transformative_Effect_of_Li_Salt_for_Pro::sec13::child1] - Operation/validation at -20 °C：All described formation and cycling (half-cell and pouch-cell) were performed at room temperature with no low-temperature data, so the -20 °C condition is not addressed.
